fullText:
Welcome to Indie App Spotlight. This is a weekly 9to5Mac series where we showcase the latest apps in the indie app world. If you’re a developer and would like your app featured, get in contact.

iOS 27 debuted to the public almost two weeks ago, with the flagship feature being Siri AI. While Siri AI was revolutionary compared to what existed prior, it still has some shortcomings. QuillCue aims to close one of the gaps with Siri AI by providing a custom keyboard that lets you save prompts for later.

Highlights

QuillCue is a rather great concept. Using custom keyboards on iOS, it allows you to insert fully prewritten prompts into Siri AI. Just swipe down from the top of your screen, switch over to the custom keyboard, select your prompt, and press enter.

It saves a lot of time if you have Siri questions you end up asking regularly, but don’t want to always type the same thing over and over again. One of the default prompts is finding nearby coffee shops that allow laptops for remote work. Since this is dependent on location, it’s always great to fetch new results that you might’ve not known about. 

Of course, you can pre-write any prompt that Siri AI can handle. QuillCue just saves you the hassle of having to respeak or retype it every single time, making Siri AI a lot easier to use.

If you end up writing a rather lengthy prompt full of different steps, QuillCue can save you a lot of time – since Siri AI doesn’t currently have a concept of ‘skills’ or learning from your usage. The possibilities are really endless. The app also offers folders for sorting your different prompts.

Lastly, it also offers the ability to import and export prompt libraries, so if you’d like to share prompts with friends or transfer them between devices, you can do so easily.

Download the app

QuillCue is available for free on the App Store, with no ads or in app purchases. You can follow the developer Parker Ortolani on X for updates. 

It requires an iPhone running iOS 27.0 or later, and is currently limited to users in the United States.

title: Feature Request: One change for the most important use of Notify Me
snippet: A key new feature in macOS 27 is Safari’s Notify Me function. This has the Apple Intelligence automatically monitor a web page for updates and send a notification when it occurs. This feature can be useful in a wide variety of ways, with price drops being one of the most obvious. Unfortunately, a limitation means that it doesn’t yet support what I would consider the most important use case for Notify Me … more…
fullText:
A key new feature in macOS 27 is Safari’s Notify Me function. This has the Apple Intelligence automatically monitor a web page for updates and send a notification when it occurs.

This feature can be useful in a wide variety of ways, with price drops being one of the most obvious. Unfortunately, a limitation means that it doesn’t yet support what I would consider the most important use case for Notify Me …

Given that computers were supposed to automate boring tasks so that humans didn’t have to do them, it’s somewhat disappointing just how frequently we find ourselves doing tedious and repetitive tasks that somehow can’t yet be easily automated. AI is changing this, and Apple’s Notify Me feature in Safari is a good example.

For example, if I’m waiting for a product to come back into stock in order to place an order, or delaying my purchase until the price drops to a more reasonable level, Safari can now monitor a web page and let me know when it’s time to buy.

But the single most tedious manual refreshing of websites I do on a regular basis is waiting for tickets to go on sale. There are some events that sell out within minutes of ticket sales opening, and as they frequently don’t happen exactly at the promised time, I often find myself visiting a website a few minutes before sales are supposed to begin and then repeatedly refreshing the page. 

In some cases, the sales window can open 20 or 30 minutes later than promised, so this process can grow extremely time-consuming and tedious. This is a perfect use case for the Notify Me feature.

Unfortunately, it can’t be used for this because the highest frequency check I can set is hourly. By the time Safari notifies me, there’s a high chance that all tickets would be sold out, or at least the ones for the seats that I really wanted.

I’d like one simple change: the ability to set the check frequency to every minute or even every 15 seconds.

I appreciate that people doing this for an extended period could effectively amount to a denial of service attack on a website, so Apple would have to impose limits on its use. A simple one would be to allow high-frequency checks to run for a maximum period of 30 minutes. Given that we wouldn’t typically need to check the same website very often, the company could even have a reset time of a month before we can use the feature again on the same website.

Is there something you’d like to see? Please take our poll and share your thoughts in the comments.

title: Craig Federighi on how Apple helps developers make the most of the iPhone Duo [Video]
snippet: Apple software chief Craig Federighi said in an interview that he is excited to see what developers will do with the hinge mechanism in the iPhone Duo. He said an API lets developers read the angle of the hinge with an accuracy of around five degrees, and the ability to read what Apple describes as the “pose” of the device … more…
fullText:
Apple software chief Craig Federighi said in an interview that he is excited to see what developers will do with the hinge mechanism in the iPhone Duo.

He said an API lets developers read the angle of the hinge with an accuracy of around five degrees, and the ability to read what Apple describes as the “pose” of the device …

Apple itself uses the hinge angle in a number of ways in software, including a feature that became an instant hit: the way the outer screen defocuses into a preview of the inner one as you open the phone. He told Donald Decodes that the feature is subtle but magical.

The goal was not a fancy animation you’d think about, but something you’d perceive automatically: the screen becomes translucent, a window to what’s below. Fundamental to the device is continuity between your experience when it’s closed and what you find when you open it. Seeing through the screen above to what’s about to be revealed below eases that journey in the most natural way. We’re really delighted with how it came out. It’s subtle but magical.

Federighi says he is confident that developers will do creative and exciting things with the hinge information exposed, just as they have with other iPhone data made available to them.

For most developers […] we’re focused on communicating the pose of the device: are you in book pose, on-table pose, tent pose? Developers don’t have to work with how many degrees open it is. By communicating the pose, the frameworks can react automatically and deliver a consistent experience across apps. But for creative experiences, like our own animation, developers can get closer to the raw information […]

We have a long history of exposing gyroscope and accelerometer data to developers, and they’ve made really interesting use of it over time. One of the ways this device expresses itself is through its poses and the hinge, and we’re excited to see what developers do with it.

He said Apple has also worked hard to make it easier for developers to create apps that take full advantage of the iPhone Duo’s capabilities.

We’ve built our platform on high-level frameworks like UIKit and SwiftUI that abstract away many of the harder layout problems, so apps often inherit new behaviors automatically. Over time we’ve added more high-level constructs that adapt automatically, which makes this transition nearly automatic for many developers.

He added that Apple also supports agentic coding tools to enable developers to adapt existing apps almost completely automatically. You can watch the interview below.

fullText:
9to5Mac is brought to you by CleanMyMac by MacPaw. With the release of macOS 27 Golden Gate, use CleanMyMac first to free up space, optimize your system, and ensure your new Mac runs at 100% on day one. Learn more.

Apple has released macOS 27 Golden Gate to the public after several months of beta testing. The update is headlined by Siri AI, but there are also Apple Intelligence enhancements to many of Apple’s own Mac apps. Here are a few of my favorites.

Apple Intelligence in macOS 27 

One of the best things about Apple’s strategy with Apple Intelligence is how it sprinkles AI-powered features throughout system apps across all of its platforms. The Mac is a great example of this, and macOS 27 takes things up a notch.

Photos

In the Photos app, there are multiple new editing tools powered by Apple Intelligence. Spatial Reframing lets you change the perspective of an image after it’s been taken, while Extend lets you expand an image across its original edges. There’s also a more powerful version of Clean Up for removing objects and people from an image after the fact.

Safari

In Safari, Apple has added several new intelligence features. You can now automatically group your tabs by topics. Using the new Notify Me feature in Safari, you can get push notifications when changes are made to a website. This is great for tracking price changes or restocks of sold-out products.

Describe an Extension might be my favorite feature in macOS 27. It lets you create a custom extension for Safari just by using a natural language prompt.

Shortcuts

Shortcuts can be a powerful way to create automations on your Mac. In macOS 27, Apple has made the process of creating shortcuts much easier. You can now use natural language to describe the shortcut you want, and Shortcuts will automatically create it.

You can even iterate on that shortcut using natural language. You can also, of course, still manually create a shortcut.

Finder

Apple has even added new Apple Intelligence features to Finder on the Mac. When naming a fold or file, you can now get suggestions powered by Apple Intelligence. So based on the content of the document or file, macOS 27 will suggest a name.

Wrap up

macOS 27 is available to Mac users everywhere. The update is supported on all Apple Silicon-powered Macs.

title: Google Health 5.09 rolling out: Cardio Load from third-party workouts, more
snippet: Following yesterday’s announcement, Google Health 5.09 is rolling out with support for the new Health Guardian features on the Pixel Watch. more…
fullText:
Following yesterday’s announcement, Google Health 5.09 is rolling out with support for the new Health Guardian features on the Pixel Watch.

With version 5.09 for Android, Pixel Watch 3, 4, and 5 users can set up blood pressure trends, insulin resistance trends, and sleep breathing quality metrics. The first monthly Health Guardian summary will appear at the beginning of October, while you can also find information in the Health tab afterwards:

Blood pressure trends, that allow you to track blood pressure patterns before they can put strain on your heart, will be available in the Heart section of the Health tab if you’ve worn your watch for 5 or more consecutive days in September.

Insulin resistance trends will be available in the Metabolic section of the Health tab if you’ve worn your watch for 7 or more days and nights in September.

Sleep breathing quality metrics, so you can learn how your sleep breathing patterns can affect your daily energy, will be available in the Sleep tab and Respiratory section of the Health tab. You’ll be able to see both daily and monthly trends.

There are also three other sets of improvements with Google Health 5.09 on Android and iOS:

Cardio Load for Workouts Started in Other Apps

	

Since launch, Google Health has allowed you to connect your favorite apps and devices to the Google Health experience. Now, the workouts you track in other apps and devices and sync to Google Health can count toward your Cardio Load, as long as the other app or device has tracked your heart rate data during that workout. This means workouts you track on other wearables like a Garmin or Apple Watch and sync to Google Health will earn Cardio Load.

Nutrition Improvements

When creating a custom food, you can now toggle food serving units and meal time more easily.

We’ve resolved an issue with custom food creation on iOS and fixed a bug where deleted items could still appear in your custom food list.

Activity and Fitness Updates

You now have more options for how you log your completed activities on the Fitness tab. Tap the “Log activity” button to see them all.

We’ve fixed an issue where some historical step streaks were missing. We are now restoring this data, and your missing streaks will reappear soon.”

title: Fireflies adds dictation to its desktop notetaking apps
snippet: Fireflies said that it won't charge extra for the new dictation feature, which can be used with any desktop app.
fullText:
Voice AI has gained particular traction for a few consumer use cases: The biggest category is meeting note-taking, and the other is AI-powered dictation, in which filter words are removed and the text is formatted neatly. Fireflies.ai, having gained a solid foothold in the meeting note-taking space, is now venturing into dictation by way of a new feature on its Mac and Windows apps.

Called Fireflies Talk, the dictation feature works just like any of the others on the market like Wispr Flow, Willow or SuperWhisper. Users can press the Fn key on Mac or Ctrl + Win on Windows to start speaking, no matter which app is open, and Fireflies will record their voice and transcribe it neatly in the text field of the app.

“People speak roughly 3x faster than they type, and voice is a much more natural way to get work done. Meetings were just the starting point; the bigger vision has always been Fred as your AI teammate throughout the day. Talk takes Fireflies beyond meetings into email, Slack, docs, prompts, and wherever else you work,” Fireflies CEO Krish Ramineni told TechCrunch over email.

The company has bundled the dictation into its existing subscription plans rather than charging for it separately. This is not entirely a new strategy. Wispr took the opposite route, releasing its meeting notetaker for free for its existing dictation app users. Speechify has also introduced dictation capabilities across different apps.

Fireflies said that the company doesn’t keep any recordings and stores dictation transcripts locally. 

Like other meeting notetakers and productivity suites, Fireflies is aiming to automate workflows based on meeting transcriptions and the context it builds on its users, and has plans to build an assistant that taps that context. 

Last year, the company introduced “mini-apps” to extract insights in different ways from meetings, and last month, it launched a feature to manage your inbox and draft emails on your behalf.

snippet: Firefox will look a little different the next time you launch it - more bubbly, with some new pops of color. fullText:
Stevie Bonifield

 

is a news writer covering all things consumer tech. Stevie started out at Laptop Mag writing news and reviews on hardware, gaming, and AI.

Firefox will look a little different the next time you launch it — more bubbly, with some new pops of color. The browser’s latest update brings a design overhaul to all desktop and mobile users, aimed at modernizing Firefox with bubble-like tabs, a rounded address bar, and refreshed colors, icons, and themes. The desktop and mobile versions of the browser will also now share the same design language. According to Mozilla, the design changes will have “no cost to your browser performance.”

1/3Firefox’s new look has more rounded UI elements.  Image: Mozilla

Mozilla says the overhauled design is a “renewal” for Firefox, following major updates over the last year, like homepage widgets, Split View, a built-in VPN, and controls for disabling the browser’s AI features. Firefox isn’t avoiding AI, though — it also launched its Smart Window AI mode earlier this year, which could help it compete with rivals’ AI browser features, like those in Chrome. With its rounded UI elements, Firefox now visually resembles Chrome a bit more, too.

The design revamp also introduces more customization options, including more themes and wallpapers to choose from. Mozilla shared a peek at some of the updated theme options in May, including a dozen different colors to choose from, each with a light and dark mode. Along with the design overhaul, Firefox 157 brings the return of an old feature: Compact Mode, back after user requests. This condensed version of Firefox “reduces the size of your tabs and toolbar to give more of your screen to the web, with an auto-compact option for smaller screens.”

title: Aurora CFO says 30,000 driverless trucks by 2030 isn’t as far-fetched as it sounds
snippet: Self-driving truck company Aurora laid out an audacious plan for 2030. Its CFO says its targets aren't aspirational.
fullText:
Autonomous vehicle technology company Aurora told investors last week that it expects to have more than 30,000 self-driving trucks on the road generating $5 billion in annual revenue by the end of 2030 — an audacious plan considering it expects to end 2026 with just 200 driverless trucks and an $80 million revenue run rate.

CFO David Maday contends the seemingly outsized target isn’t as large or as out of reach as it might appear.

“While 30,000 kind of feels like a lot — and it does in the autonomy space for sure — in terms of trucks relative to the overall market, it’s kind of pretty small,” he told TechCrunch in a recent interview, adding that the four major truck manufacturers produce anywhere between 250,000 and 300,000 new trucks a year. “I don’t think it’s aspirational,” he added, “I think we can do it.”

Investors haven’t exactly embraced Aurora’s 2030 vision. Shares have continued to slide since the company’s annual analyst and investor day on September 23. On Monday, shares closed down 12.42%, to $5.29.

But investors have time to come around and, according to Maday, the big “unlock” for Aurora starts in 2027 and accelerates from there. The company expects to go from 200 driverless trucks at the end of 2026 to more than 1,000 a year later.

Today, Aurora operates what it calls a transportation-as-a-service business — a proof-of-concept model that it plans to limit to about 500 trucks. It owns and operates the self-driving trucks and charges its customers, including Detmar Logistics, Hirschbach, McLane, and Werner about a $2 per mile, a rate that includes a fuel surcharge.

That works out to roughly the same rates as other carriers’ typical pricing. The real shift — and the real savings, Maday says — will happen next year as when Aurora begins moving to a driver-as-a-service model. Instead of Aurora owning the trucks, customers will buy the self-driving trucks and pay Aurora a per-mile subscription fee for the self-driving technology, which the company expects to be about $0.85. Under this model, the customers will own and maintain the truck, while Aurora maintains the self-driving system and its accompanying hardware.

Moving the trucks off Aurora’s balance sheet is critical if the company wants to scale — and it’s likely what investors are paying attention to. The company said it expects to reach breakeven gross margins (meaning revenue would cover the direct costs of running the trucks) on a run-rate basis in the first half of 2027 with around 500 trucks on the road.

The next big leap comes at the end of 2027 with Aurora’s third-generation hardware— the sensors, computers, and other equipment that let its trucks drive themselves — which will be mass-produced autonomous vehicle hardware built by its partner, Aumovio (formerly known as Continental). Aumovio isn’t just engineering and manufacturing the hardware kit; the company is also financing it for Aurora — easing the financial burden on the self-driving truck company. Aumovio will also service and repair the kits for customers.

Aurora plans to expand its operations at the same time. By 2030, the company expects to grow beyond a few states in the South to the vast majority of the continental U.S., according to Maday.

“By 2028, I expect that our cost structures are going to be really outstanding, that’s why you see our gross margin starting to take off …” Maday said. “Once you get to that point, I think going into ride hailing is fine,” he said, confirming that Aurora still plans to eventually enter the robotaxi market.

		Kirsten Korosec is a reporter and editor who has covered the future of transportation from EVs and autonomous vehicles to urban air mobility and in-car tech for more than a decade. She is currently the transportation editor at TechCrunch and co-host of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast. She is also co-founder and co-host of the podcast, “The Autonocast.” She previously wrote for Fortune, The Verge, Bloomberg, MIT Technology Review and CBS Interactive.

title: Apple has big October coming for new hardware and software, here’s the lineup
snippet: Apple has a big October ahead, with several major hardware and software launches coming. Here’s everything to expect from Apple in October. more…
fullText:
Apple has a big October ahead, with several major hardware and software launches coming. Here’s everything to expect from Apple in October.

iPhone Duo launches October 23

iPhone Duo is confirmed to arrive in users’ hands in October. Pre-orders open Friday, October 16 and the first units deliver on October 23.

Apple’s first foldable model might be limited in supply. However, iPhone Duo is launching in lots of countries simultaneously, which could be a good sign for availability. Per Apple:

Customers in more than 70 countries and regions, including Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, Colombia, France, Germany, India, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, Singapore, South Korea, Türkiye, the UAE, the UK, the U.S., and Vietnam, will be able to pre-order iPhone Duo beginning at 5 a.m. PT on Friday, October 16, with availability beginning Friday, October 23. iPhone Duo will be available in 28 other countries and regions beginning Friday, October 30.

If iPhone Duo supply was expected to be significantly lower than anticipated demand, it’s unlikely Apple would launch the product in close to 100 countries and regions right away.

Read more: Apple unveils foldable iPhone Duo

Hardware rumors: New Macs, Home products, and iPad mini

Apple reportedly has a lot more new hardware products launching in October too. We’re expecting new Macs, Home products, and an upgraded iPad mini. Here’s what’s rumored:

Touchscreen MacBook Pro / Ultra: All-new design for high-end MacBook with OLED, more

M6 iMac: Powerful chip and new color options

M6 MacBook Pro: Update for 14-inch base MacBook Pro

New Apple TV 4K: A19 or A19 Pro chip, Siri AI, new Siri Remote

HomePad: New home hub with built-in touchscreen

HomePod mini 2: More powerful chip, audio upgrades, more

iPad mini: OLED display, A19 Pro or A20 Pro chip

Two standout products include the first touchscreen Mac, which could be branded MacBook Pro or Ultra, and the long-expected home hub ‘HomePad.’ Everything else will be smaller updates to existing products.

Software launches: iOS 27.1 and iOS 27.2, more

Apple has confirmed that iPhone Duo will run on iOS 27.1 when it launches in October. 

It’s speculated that 27.1 will be Duo-exclusive. However, it might come to other iPhones too, but only include bug fixes or security updates while the majority of changes are for Apple’s foldable.

Normally we would expect more features in iOS 27.1, but in an unusual move, iOS 27.2 is already in testing and is also expected to arrive in October. As a result, iOS 27.2 is likely intended for all iPhones while 27.1 is primarily for iPhone Duo. 

New features in iOS 27.2 so far include:

Profiles for the Apple TV app come to iPhone and iPad

Dual Capture feature available for Group FaceTime calls

Siri AI expands to several new languages

New features for Apple Music, CarPlay Ultra, and more might be coming too

When iOS 27 launched, Apple confirmed that Siri AI “will expand to French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish next month.“ Since that language expansion is included in iOS 27.2, we’re expecting both 27.1 and 27.2 to arrive before October ends.

The iOS 27.2 beta also includes an all-new Health app with Apple Intelligence features, but it’s expected to be removed from the shipping version and return in iOS 27.3 later this year instead.

Read more: Here’s everything new Apple TV has coming in October

Which new hardware and software launches in October are you most excited for? Let us know in the comments.

title: Apple’s Taptic Engine patent defeat sends litigation funder’s shares up 9%
snippet: Shares in litigation funder Burford Capital jumped more than 9% today as a result of Apple’s $5.7 billion verdict over Taptic Engine patent infringement. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Shares in litigation funder Burford Capital jumped more than 9% today as a result of Apple’s $5.7 billion verdict over Taptic Engine patent infringement. Here are the details.

Apple verdict lifts litigation funder valuation

Last Friday, a US jury ruled that Apple’s Taptic Engine infringes on two patents held by California-based company Taction Technology.

Apple introduced the Taptic Engine in September 2014 with the first Apple Watch, and the technology has since expanded to other products, including the iPhone, where it provides haptic feedback for notifications, interactions, and other system events.

When Taction filed its patent infringement lawsuit in 2021, the company accused Apple of directly and indirectly infringing two of its patents through the Taptic Engine used in a range of iPhone and Apple Watch models.

Last Friday, following the verdict, Taction said the jury had “vindicated its patent rights,” while Apple said it strongly disagreed with the decision and would appeal.

Earlier today, as reported by The Financial Times, litigation funder Burford Capital disclosed that it has a financial entitlement in the case, and that it could be entitled to $1.4 billion if the $5.7 billion verdict is ultimately paid in full.

The disclosure sent Burford shares sharply higher in London, with the stock closing up 9.41% and giving the company a market capitalization of £659.9 million, or roughly $875 million.

Bloomberg Law notes that court records show that Taction received funding from Kenosha Investments LP and Gronostaj Investments LLC. The report also notes that Kenosha has been identified as an indirect subsidiary of Burford, which finances lawsuits in exchange for a share of any eventual recovery.

In a statement to investors on Monday, Burford said that if the $5.7 billion verdict were paid in full, its $1.4 billion entitlement would be split roughly equally between the company’s own balance sheet and its investment funds.

title: Apple faces class action over Apple Pay fees charged to card issuers
snippet: U.S. District Judge Jeffrey S. White has certified a class-action lawsuit accusing Apple of charging payment card issuers inflated fees for Apple Pay transactions. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
U.S. District Judge Jeffrey S. White has certified a class-action lawsuit accusing Apple of charging payment card issuers inflated fees for Apple Pay transactions. Here are the details.

As first spotted by AppleInsider, a federal judge has allowed an antitrust lawsuit over Apple Pay fees to proceed as a class action, meaning payment card issuers across the U.S. may now pursue their claims against Apple as a group.

In a press release from Hagens Berman, the law firm representing the plaintiffs, the firm said the certified class includes all U.S. entities that issued payment cards enabled for Apple Pay and paid Apple fees on transactions made with those cards.

The firm argues that while mobile wallets on Android do not charge card issuers transaction fees, Apple charges U.S. issuers 0.15% on credit card transactions and 0.5 cents on debit card transactions made through Apple Pay.

From the press release:

The lawsuit accuses Apple of extracting up to $1 billion annually in fees in violation of federal antitrust law. Apple denies rivals access to the technology needed to develop a competing mobile wallet, according to the class action. On iOS devices, Apple has ensured that only its mobile wallet, Apple Pay, can make contactless payments at the point of sale. Having secured a monopoly for Apple Pay in this fashion, Apple charges card issuers who use Apple Pay, like credit unions and other small financial institutions, supracompetitive fees for a service that is available on Android devices for free, according to the lawsuit.

The firm also highlighted that Judge White “denied Apple’s motion to exclude expert testimony attorneys say establishes common proof that Apple maintains monopoly power in a relevant antitrust aftermarket for tap-and-pay iOS mobile wallets as well as a broader market for all mobile wallets.”

The lawsuit seeks reimbursement for card issuers that paid Apple Pay fees, as well as an injunction against Apple’s challenged policies.

title: Apple has three products launching soon that we’ve waited a long time for
snippet: Apple had a big September, but it’s set to keep momentum going in October with several rumored product unveilings soon that we’ve waited a long time for. more…
fullText:
Apple had a big September, but it’s set to keep momentum going in October with several rumored product unveilings soon that we’ve waited a long time for.

#1: MacBook Pro / Ultra redesign with touchscreen

The Mac is a long-time touchscreen holdout, but that’s finally set to change with a new MacBook Pro (or MacBook Ultra) product expected to launch in October.

Apple’s next-gen MacBook Pro will introduce a brand new industrial design—the first such overhaul in five years. And in addition to touch support, it will boast an OLED display, Dynamic Island, and possibly a C2 cellular modem option.

It’s been a long time since the MacBook Pro got a new look. But far longer since touchscreens became the norm, and Apple decided to forego them on the Mac. I’m excited to see how touch might enhance the experience of the Mac moving forward.

#2: New Apple TV 4K

There’s never been a longer wait for new Apple TV hardware than the current drought of updates. Apple’s latest model, the third-gen Apple TV 4K, was introduced in 2022.

Rumors indicate we’ll finally get a new Apple TV 4K in October, headlined by a powerful A19 or A19 Pro chip and Siri AI support.

This summer Apple raised prices on most of its products, including the Apple TV. That means the four-year-old Apple TV 4K now costs $199—far more than the $129 price it launched at. Here’s hoping the new Apple TV doesn’t go any higher.

#3: ‘HomePad’

Rumors of a HomePod with a display have been around for nearly as long as the HomePod’s existence. But they ramped up in 2024 when Mark Gurman offered an in-depth report on what’s commonly called the ‘HomePad.’

	

HomePad is a smart display with built-in speaker that will reportedly spearhead Apple’s renewed push into home products. It will have a new OS that resembles parts of iOS, tvOS, and watchOS, including a StandBy-like mode.

Siri AI is expected to be central to the product, which will also feature a camera, customizable widgets, and built-in Apple apps like Photos, Notes, Music, Calendar, and more.

title: Motorola Signature 27 confirmed to support GrapheneOS
snippet: It’s confirmed: The mysterious Motorola phone getting support for the privacy-focused GrapheneOS will be the Motorola Signature 27 that was announced earlier this week. more…
fullText:
It’s confirmed: The mysterious Motorola phone getting support for the privacy-focused GrapheneOS will be the Motorola Signature 27 that was announced earlier this week.

GrapheneOS, a privacy-focused take on Android that’s grown popular in recent years, has so far only been available on Pixel devices. That’s for a number of reasons relating back to how Google handles the software and the security components in Pixel (and Tensor) hardware.

But, now, GrapheneOS is officially stepping beyond Pixel and into a device that will come pre-loaded with its version of Android. It was announced that this would be a Motorola device, but which device was left a mystery as all existing Motorola devices were not compatible with the platform.

Unsurprisingly, though, the first GrapheneOS device from Motorola will be the Motorola Signature 27. GrapheneOS confirmed the news on Twitter/X, though other details are still minimal. It’s apparently still planned that devices will be sold with GrapheneOS pre-installed. The Signature 27 was announced earlier this week and its use of the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset is likely a major part of the reason it will be able to run GrapheneOS properly.

	

An exact release date for the Motorola Signature 27 has yet to be confirmed, and it’s unclear if GrapheneOS will be available right away either. It’s already known that future versions of Razr flip and Razr Fold will also support the privacy-focused OS.

title: VW Previews ID Tiguan Electric SUV to Replace ID 4 in 2027
snippet: The electric SUV is set to make its full debut in early October before arriving in the US next year.
fullText:
German automaker Volkswagen gave us our first camouflaged look at the newest member of its electric vehicle lineup on Monday morning. Dubbed the ID Tiguan, the compact electric SUV is set to replace the current VW ID 4 EV, with an “early 2027” launch in Europe and a US arrival later.

The ID Tiguan follows the ID Polo and ID Cross as the third electric vehicle in VW’s global portfolio to be renamed and brought in line with the brand’s combustion and hybrid models. Volkswagen says the rename — basically calling it an electric variant of the familiar Tiguan — makes it easier for customers to understand the vehicle’s size and capabilities, and to set their expectations, than the abstract numeral 4 does. I’m inclined to agree.

Two different versions of the ID Tiguan were previewed. Could one be a styling package or, perhaps, a sporty performance model?Volkswagen

VW previewed the EV in yellow camouflage, hinting at proportions and details that are, unsurprisingly, similar to those of the current-generation Tiguan. The headlamps and light signature — visible through small cutouts in the camo — appear sharper and more angular, while the tail lights have a more geometric appearance than the combustion car. It’s safe to assume a touch more care has been paid to aerodynamics, since EVs generally need smaller grilles than combustion cars, but the overall shape and sculpting are largely spot-on to the Tiguan you can find at dealerships today.

			

More from CNET

Two versions of the ID Tiguan appear in the preview: likely a standard configuration and a sporty variant with unique wheels and what appears to be the Tiguan’s more aggressive R-Line bumper. On the combustion model, this indicates either the R-Line styling package or a higher-powered Tiguan Turbo spec. 

If this is the latter, I’m curious whether VW will use the “ID Tiguan Turbo” name for the hot crossover. Yes, I know that EVs don’t use turbochargers, but the automaker has told me previously that its use of “Turbo” on the combustion Tiggy denotes increased performance, not the presence of a turbocharger. It could apply that same logic to naming the EV. (Likewise, VW’s cousin, Porsche, has called its high-performance electric sedan the Taycan Turbo for years, despite it also lacking a turbocharger, so a precedent has been set.)

The new electric Tiguan will reach Europe in early 2027, with the US to follow.Volkswagen

The ID Tiguan will replace the ID 4 in the US and will be sold alongside the combustion and hybrid-electric Tiguan models. VW hasn’t released any details on the ID Tiguan’s electric powertrain, performance or range, but the current ID 4 offers a decent baseline for speculating about improvements. Expect more concrete specs when the ID Tiguan makes its world premiere in “early October,” according to the release.

A VW representative told CNET via email that the brand would share North American timing and additional market-specific details “following its European launch in early 2027.” So, it may be some time before details of the US rollout solidify. I’ve a hunch that VW is waiting to see what happens with the US EV market over the next few months before committing to a plan.

VW isn’t the only traditional automaker rechristening its EVs. Mercedes-Benz’s next generation of electric vehicles will largely drop the EQx naming (EQE, EQA, EQG, etc.) in favor of names that align with the brand’s traditional “Class” names of its combustion cars (C-Class, CLA-Class, G-Class and so on), using the “with EQ Technology” suffix to denote a battery-electric powertrain.

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Antuan Goodwin
						

						

							Senior Writer, Electrified Cars						
					

											

								

											Antuan has nearly 20 years of expertise and experience testing hundreds of cars, including electric, hybrid, plug-in hybrid, hydrogen, and traditional combustion vehicles.

title: SpaceX Hits Major Milestone, Launching Starship Into Orbit for First Time
snippet: The world’s largest launch vehicle ever delivers 26 of the most advanced Starlink satellites into space.
fullText:
Despite an engine shutting down too soon, Elon Musk’s SpaceX managed to get its Starship into Earth orbit for the first time ever. The aerospace manufacturer and satellite communications company also deployed dozens of Starlink’s most advanced satellites into orbit on Monday.

The Starship launched at 8:48 a.m. ET at SpaceX’s Starbase in Boca Chica Beach, Texas. The noncrewed orbit was planned to last 10 hours — consisting of six laps around Earth — but the SpaceX control team decided to cut the flight to three hours. After reentering Earth’s atmosphere, the Starship splashed down in the Pacific Ocean north of Hawaii at 11:58 a.m. ET, tipping over and erupting into flames.

For the most part, it was mission accomplished for the 14th launch of the Starship, which, at 407 feet tall, is the largest launch vehicle ever designed, 44 feet taller than NASA’s retired Saturn V. After reaching orbit Monday, the Starship jettisoned 26 of the newest and most updated Starlink satellites into orbit, adding to the more than 11,000 already floating around above.

			

More from CNET

The Starship reached an altitude of 170 miles and sped along at 17,500mph.

Of the previous 13 Starship test flights, several ended in crashes over the Indian Ocean, either intentionally caused by SpaceX or accidentally. No one has ever been hurt by the crashes.

Monday’s achievement almost didn’t happen. Before reaching orbit, one of the Starship’s more than three dozen engines went kaput, but SpaceX engineers decided to continue the flight after conferring for several minutes. SpaceX did not say whether the engine shutdown was a factor in the decision to reduce the trip from 10 hours to three.

SpaceX had launched its Starship 13 times before Monday’s orbital flight.Ronaldo Schemidt/AFP/Getty Images

Ultimately, Musk and SpaceX want the Starship to be fully reusable to save on launch costs — what goes up will come down intact. If all goes as planned, the first-stage booster that provides lift-off thrust would return to the launch site after separating from the main Starship. The Starship would also return to Earth, landing vertically.

SpaceX wants to have the Starship certified by NASA in time for the agency’s Artemis III mission, which could be next summer. In that mission, a NASA Orion capsule with astronauts on board will dock with Jeff Bezos’ Blue Moon and later with Musk’s Starship.

In the Artemis IV mission, slated for 2028 at the earliest, astronauts will land on the moon in either the Blue Moon or Starship. The overall plan is for moon landings to alternate between the two spacecraft on subsequent trips.

SpaceX is planning to add two more launch sites: one at Florida’s Kennedy Space Center and another in Vermilion Parish along the Gulf Coast of Louisiana.

Expanding Starlink coverage

Although Musk originally eyed the Starship as a method to reach Mars — and possibly carry humans there as colonists — his primary goal now is to keep putting Starlink satellites into orbit, more than 100,000 of them. 

Starlink could have the newly launched V3 satellites online and serving customers within weeks. SpaceX says the updated satellites provide a downlink of 1 terabyte per second, a 10-fold increase from V2 satellites, and also an uplink capacity 22 times greater. Downlink refers to data transmitted “down” to Earth, and uplink is the other way around.

SpaceX says the V3 satellites will improve direct-to-device connectivity, also called direct-to-cell, which is the link between satellites and cell phones. The company says it will benefit customers on ships at sea, in many rural areas and during emergencies, where there might not be access to high-speed internet.

Pointing to the future 

The Starship launch was an exciting sign for the future, former astronaut Mike Massimino told CNET. “Astro Mike” did two missions to the Hubble Telescope and was the first person to tweet from space. He was also a recurring character on the TV show Big Bang Theory and is a professor at Columbia University.

“This enables companies and individuals to think what they might do in space, not necessarily tourism but access to getting larger things into space,” Massimino told CNET. “This is a really big rocket and can launch large things into space.”

Massimino said that no one could have expected, 15 years ago, the sort of growth we’re seeing now. Putting power systems and data centers into space is a realistic goal, as more and more companies invest in space exploration.

“Some entrepreneurs had the foresight to see that if you give people access, the demand will come. People will think it’s more affordable to do a project in space,” Massimo said. “We have 14,000 working satellites and we’re headed toward 200,000. It’s truly amazing.”

fullText:
Andrew Liszewski

 

is a senior reporter who’s been covering and reviewing the latest gadgets and tech since 2006, but has loved all things electronic since he was a kid.

Following leaks revealing a major redesign earlier this month and an official teaser posted to X yesterday, Fairphone has shared some exclusive details with The Verge about the first follow-up to its Fairbuds wireless earbuds that debuted over two years ago.

A full reveal of the Fairbuds 2 is planned for October 14th, but we can confirm the new version will carry forward the same focus on repairability that made the original Fairbuds so unique with “seven fully replaceable and modular parts.” The new Fairbuds 2 will also expand their Bluetooth capabilities with added support for Sony’s high-resolution and adaptive LDAC codec. The original Fairbuds only supported the SBC and AAC codecs, similar to Apple’s AirPods.

Fairphone says the Fairbuds 2 will launch in Europe first for €119, followed by a US release where they’ll be available for $119. The first-generation Fairbuds were priced at €149 when they debuted in 2024, or around $162 at the time, but have since come down in price to $99.99 in the US.

title: OpenAI reportedly ditches model over safety concerns
snippet: A top executive at the AI lab told the Wall Street Journal that the model in question had displayed a poor aptitude for following orders.
fullText:
In Brief

Posted:

4:39 PM PDT · September 28, 2026

Image Credits:Samuel Boivin/NurPhoto / Getty Images

		

							

											
									

					

	

OpenAI had planned to release yet another AI model next month, but has decided to nix the release over safety concerns.

The Wall Street Journal reports that Astra 6.1 was scheduled to be released as soon as within the next few days. However, the model “showed higher levels of deception” than previous models and exhibited unsafe behavior, the Journal writes.

Saachi Jain, OpenAI’s head of safety systems, told the WSJ that the model tested poorly on alignment, a measure of how well the program adheres to human intent.

TechCrunch reached out to OpenAI for more information and will update the article if it responds.

Astra was released earlier this month and hailed by OpenAI as its most powerful model yet. 

Questions about safety have plagued the AI industry over the past several months — ever since the Hugging Face incident, in which an OpenAI agent broke free of its sandboxed environment and hacked several different companies. Since that incident, more models — including Anthropic’s Claude and Google’s Gemini — have been revealed to have exhibited similar behavior. 

The deluge of concerning stories has, ironically, helped to push the policy conversation in the U.S. toward an outcome desired by top AI labs: the institution of new industry standards for AI safety and potentially a slowdown of the industry itself.

Companies like OpenAI and Anthropic have claimed that the concern here is safety, although another potential motivation posited by critics is that it could entrench the industry position of those companies at the detriment of less resourced firms.

title: Opera’s free built-in VPN can now turn on automatically when using public Wi-Fi
snippet: Opera announced today that its free, built-in VPN for desktop can now automatically activate when users connect to public or unsecured Wi-Fi networks. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Opera announced today that its free, built-in VPN for desktop can now automatically activate when users connect to public or unsecured Wi-Fi networks. Here are the details.

Opt-in feature rolls out today in the US and France

Since 2016, the Opera browser has offered a free, built-in VPN. The company says this builds on its core belief that “making basic online privacy accessible to everyone.”

In recent years, VPNs have gone from being a relatively niche privacy tool to something much more mainstream. Still, according to data from We Are Social’s Digital 2026 Mid-Year Global Update Report, only 23% of internet users aged 16 and older use a VPN for at least some of their online activities.

That is a problem, particularly for users who rely on public Wi-Fi for work or while traveling.

Today, Opera announced that users in the US and France can opt to have its built-in VPN turn on automatically whenever they connect to a public or unsecured Wi-Fi network.

Here’s Opera:

Public Wi-Fi networks are notoriously vulnerable to snooping and data interception. Opera’s browser VPN now removes manual friction by automatically activating when detecting public or unsecured Wi-Fi networks. Users can study, work, manage finances, or browse without having to remember to turn on protection manually. To respect user agency, the feature remains strictly opt-in and can be easily toggled within settings. This functionality is rolling out today to Opera users in the US and France.

Opera notes that its “free VPN operates under strict GDPR laws,” adding that it “has been independently audited by Deloitte.” The company also stresses that the VPN is part of a broader set of built-in privacy tools, alongside Opera’s native Ad Blocker and Tracker Blocker.

title: New iPad mini coming soon with these major changes
snippet: Apple is about to release a new iPad mini. This will mark the first update to the device in two years, and it’s expected to be a big one. Here’s everything we know so far about the new iPad mini coming as soon as next month. more…
fullText:
Apple is about to release a new iPad mini. This will mark the first update to the device in two years, and it’s expected to be a big one. Here’s everything we know so far about the new iPad mini coming as soon as next month.

OLED display

By far the biggest change to the new iPad mini will be to the display. According to multiple sources, the iPad mini 8 will feature an OLED display.

This will be a dramatic improvement to the iPad mini’s current LCD panel. For users, the move to OLED means deeper blacks, richer colors, and better contrast. The iPhone X was the first iPhone to use an OLED display in 2017, while the OLED iPad Pro debuted in 2024.

One lingering question, though, is whether the new iPad mini will use a ProMotion display for refresh rates of up to 120Hz. According to a sketchy rumor last week, the new iPad mini won’t offer ProMotion support and will instead be limited to 60Hz.

This hasn’t been corroborated by any other sources, though, so I’m holding out hope this leak is incorrect.

New chip

The current iPad mini, released in October 2024, is powered by Apple’s A17 Pro chip. The new iPad mini will likely feature the A19 Pro or A20 Pro chip. This will offer a solid boost in performance, and could enable support for the most advanced Siri AI features in iOS 27.

Better water resistance

According to Bloomberg, Apple has tested a “redesigned casing” for the iPad mini that is water-resistant like the iPhone.

Whether or not this water-resistant casing pans out remains to be seen. However, it would make the iPad mini far more durable. It’d be especially notable for people who use it as an e-reader, as one of the top features of dedicated e-readers like the Kindle is water resistance.

New speaker technology

The iPad mini 8 might also be Apple’s first device with a revamped vibration-based speaker system. This vibration-based speaker system would let Apple remove speaker holes, aiding its work to make the device water-resistant.

In contrast, the iPhone has speaker holes, but Apple uses gaskets and adhesives to make the device water-resistant.

New iPad mini release date

According to the latest reporting from Bloomberg, Apple is aiming to release the OLED iPad mini as early as this October. It’s allegedly the “biggest overhaul to the iPad mini in half a decade.”

There’s no word on how much the new iPad mini will cost. Apple increased the price of the current iPad mini in July from $499 to $599 (currently discounted to $569 on Amazon). Whether the new iPad mini with OLED is even more expensive remains to be seen.

What do you think of Apple’s rumored plans for the iPad mini? Are you tempted by the OLED display? Let us know down in the comments.

title: OpenAI cancels GPT-6.1 Astra release over misbehavior & safety concerns
snippet: OpenAI has scrapped plans to release GPT-6.1 Astra in the next few weeks over concerns that the model is misbehaving. more…
fullText:
OpenAI has scrapped plans to release GPT-6.1 Astra in the next few weeks over concerns that the model is misbehaving.

The New York Times reports that OpenAI was planning to release GPT-6.1 Astra “in the coming days or weeks,” sometime in October, as its next major model release. GPT-6 Astra launched on September 3. GPT-6.1 Astra is said to have been “more capable” compared to GPT-6 in “completing challenging tasks from end-to-end without human assistance, as well as writing.”

The report cites an interview with Saachi Jain, OpenAI’s head of safety systems, who confirmed that the model had regressed in two specific areas. Firstly, it “performed poorly on tests measuring alignment,” or how closely it sticks to the commands/prompts given by the human operator. Secondly, it showed “higher levels of deception,” not always telling the truth about the actions it did or did not take following a prompt. It was also added that GPT-6.1 Astra would push forward in a task beyond the current scope and without user permission, including interacting with external tools and/or services.

The new model would have been available in both ChatGPT and Codex.

	

OpenAI is due to have its annual developer conference, DevDay, tomorrow, where it’s very possible the company may have teased this new model update. Instead, the report explains, OpenAI will shift focus to “improving the safety of future models.”

This comes at a time when both OpenAI and Anthropic are calling for a slowdown in major AI development following recent breaches in GPT and Claude. Google’s Gemini also hacked into companies like those models, but stopped those actions faster than either of its rivals.

title: You Should Download iOS 27.0.1 Now for These iPhone Fixes
snippet: The update includes a fix for a bug that might cause your touchscreen to stop working.
fullText:
Apple released iOS 27.0.1 on Monday, about two weeks after the tech giant released iOS 27. The latest update is focused on bug fixes for most iPhones, and two of those fixes are specific to the new iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max devices. Everyone should download the update to make sure their devices are running as smoothly as possible.

CNET

You can download iOS 27.0.1 now by going to Settings and tapping General. Next, select Software Update, tap Update Now and follow the prompts on your screen.

		

			

Apple wrote in the update’s release notes that iOS 27.0.1 fixes three bugs. One bug the update addresses might cause your iPhone’s touchscreen to be unresponsive if you try to open your Notification and Control centers at the same time.

The other two bugs iOS 27.0.1 addresses are iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max specific. One bug might cause those devices to restart after failing to authenticate via Face ID. Some people on Reddit ran into this issue on the new device and advised others not to set up Face ID because of the bug. Once you download this update, the bug should be fixed, and you can set up the security feature if you haven’t already.

The other bug iOS 27.0.1 addresses could cause a color artifact to appear in photos taken with certain settings.

Here are the full release notes for iOS 27.0.1.

This update provides bug fixes for your iPhone, including fixes for the following issues:

iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max may unexpectedly restart when Face ID fails to authenticate.

A color artifact may appear on photos captured at 2x under certain lighting conditions at f/1.48 on a small number of iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max devices.

Opening Notification Center and Control Center simultaneously may cause the touchscreen to become unresponsive.

For more on iOS 27, here’s what to know about the update and why you might not see iOS 27.1 on your device.

title: Google rolling out blood pressure & insulin resistance, more on Pixel Watch 3, 4, 5
snippet: As previewed during last month’s Pixel Watch 5 launch, Google is now starting to roll out blood pressure trends, insulin resistance trends, and sleep breathing quality metrics. more…
fullText:
As previewed during last month’s Pixel Watch 5 launch, Google is now starting to roll out blood pressure trends, insulin resistance trends, and sleep breathing quality metrics.

Health Guardian is Google’s overarching brand for the Pixel Watch’s suite of “proactive health and safety tools.” It includes Breathing Emergency Detection, which is available in Europe on the Pixel Watch 4 and 5.

The blood pressure trends feature works by passively measuring your pulse and motion patterns over the course of a month. It’s intended to let you detect “persistent higher cardiovascular trends early.” This works without a cuff or manual calibration, and was trained using billions of minutes of raw heart and movement data. You need “at least 5 consecutive days in a week” of data.

Insulin resistance trends analyze multi-week physiological data to track shifts in metabolic health without requiring a blood draw. Insulin resistance impacts how your body absorbs energy from food, with Google needing a minimum of 7 days of data in a month. The feature uses Google’s largest sensor foundational model. It was pre-trained using over 1 trillion minutes of data from 5 million opted-in users.

	
	

Both sets of trend insights will appear in the Google Health app on the first day of each month.

Meanwhile, sleep breathing quality metrics will track overnight breathing changes. In the morning, you’ll see how much time was spent optimally breathing, while a monthly report identifies longer-term patterns.

Pixel Watch 3, 4, and 5 users will be able to set up these three features in the Google Health app starting this week. Access is free on those three devices, with the first trend reports coming in early October.

If you’re a Google Health Premium subscriber, these three features are also coming to the Fitbit Air “later this year.”

title: Samsung’s Android 17 floodgates are open – updates rolling out for Galaxy S26, S25, more
snippet: The floodgates are open. After a delay and staggered starts, Samsung is widely rolling out its Android 17-based One UI 9 update for Galaxy S26 users around the globe, and they’re not alone. more…
fullText:
The floodgates are open. After a delay and staggered starts, Samsung is widely rolling out its Android 17-based One UI 9 update for Galaxy S26 users around the globe, and they’re not alone.

Samsung started testing its Android 17 update, otherwise known as One UI 9, back in May of this year. The stable version debuted on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Flip 8 in July, and the company announced its stable rollout to older devices would begin earlier this month. A delay behind the scenes left users waiting a bit longer, but it’s actually happening now.

That starts with Galaxy S26 devices, which are now widely receiving their Android 17 updates in regions all over the world. The update was already showing up for many in the US and South Korea, but it’s now appearing across Europe, India, and other regions as SammyGuru points out. Inbox by 9to5Google author Daniel Bader also notes that the roughly 4GB update landed on his Galaxy S26 Ultra in Canada earlier today. 

And the Galaxy S26 series is not alone.

	

SamMobile notes that stable updates are starting to appear for a host of other Galaxy devices, though right now in staggered releases and/or only for those who were previously enrolled in the beta program. Devices included in those early rollouts include Galaxy S25 series (including FE and Edge), Galaxy Z TriFold, Galaxy Z Fold 7, Galaxy Z Flip 7, and Galaxy Z Flip 7 FE.

Stay tuned as Samsung’s rollout expands – if history serves, we’ll be seeing a host of updates arriving in the coming days. Let us know in the comments if you see the update land on your device.

title: Google has fixed an issue that caused thousands of iPhone apps to crash overnight
snippet: An issue with Google’s Firebase left thousands of iPhone apps crashing overnight, but a fix has already been applied. more…
fullText:
An issue with Google’s Firebase left thousands of iPhone apps crashing overnight, but a fix has already been applied.

If you found apps on your iPhone or iPad were crashing last night, you’re not alone. Google confirmed last night that an issue with Analytics for Firebase was causing crashes when apps tried to launch. The issue was on Google’s end with an “incorrectly formatted payload” for the SDK.

You wouldn’t think of Google when a widespread crashing issue surfaces on iPhone, but Firebase is a valuable tool for developers on both Android and iOS, and is integrated into thousands of apps. The crashing issue was out of the developer’s hands and required a fix on Google’s end. The impact was huge, with some developers seeing tens of thousands of crashes – some far more – from their app’s users.

That fix has already been rolled out, Google confirmed.

	

Nick Cooke, a software engineer at Google, summarized a timeline of events:

Starting on Monday, 2026-09-28 at 17:41 US/PDT. Google Analytics for Firebase iOS+ experienced an issue causing crashes on launch due to an incorrectly formatted payload received by the SDK.

We fully rolled out a fix by Monday, 2026-09-28 at 19:52 US/PDT.

No SDK updates are required on your end to apply this fix.

Due to caching behavior, some app instances may still experience crashes for up to 4 hours after the rollout completed. These remaining cases should automatically resolve themselves by 2026-09-28 at 23:52 US/PDT.

At this point, crashing issues should be resolved. The patch for this problem was fully rolled out by around midnight Pacific Time last night; no app updates needed. Affected apps should be fully working again at this point.

9to5Mac is brought to you by CleanMyMac by MacPaw. With the release of macOS 27 Golden Gate, use CleanMyMac first to free up space, optimize your system, and ensure your new Mac runs at 100% on day one. Learn more.

One of the many new features included in macOS 27 Golden Gate is Safari’s new “Notify Me” feature, which lets users get alerted when a website updates content they’re interested in. Here’s how to use it.

Safari can now notify you when webpages change

One of the most useful ways Apple has incorporated Apple Intelligence into macOS 27 Golden Gate is through Safari’s new “Notify Me” feature.

With it, users can ask Safari to monitor a webpage for specific changes and receive a notification when it detects an update.

When setting up a new custom notification, in addition to telling Safari what to look for, the user can also set a regular schedule ranging from hourly to monthly.

After the custom notification is set up, Safari will check the webpage according to the selected schedule and notify the user when it detects the requested change, such as a price drop, an item coming back in stock, changes to policies, registrations opening, or new information being added to the page.

Setting up Safari’s new “Notify Me” feature:

On Safari, go to the webpage you want to keep an eye on.

Click the Page menu button to the right of the Smart Search field.

Select “Notify Me” from the pop-up menu.

In the “What should Safari look for?” field, describe what you want. Apple Intelligence will then analyze the page’s contents to determine whether it can handle your request.

Optionally, you can set how often and when Safari should check for updates. Hourly and Daily let you choose a specific time, while Weekly and Monthly also let you choose specific days.

Click Done. Alternatively, Safari may show a Next button instead. In that case, macOS will ask for permission to send Safari notifications. You can also manage Safari notification permissions from Settings > Notifications > Safari.

Importantly, since the feature relies on Apple Intelligence, it may not be available in all languages or regions. To check the current availability status, follow this link.

title: tvOS 27 adds new reason to use profiles on your Apple TV 4K
snippet: Apple keeps improving its profiles feature on Apple TV 4K, and a change in tvOS 27 related to app access offers another reason to use profiles. more…
fullText:
Apple keeps improving its profiles feature on Apple TV 4K, and a change in tvOS 27 related to app access offers another reason to use profiles.

tvOS 27 lets you restrict users from launching specific apps

User profiles are a common feature of every major streaming service. They ensure viewers in a shared household can keep their viewing history and recommendations separate, among other benefits.

Apple has long had a profiles feature in tvOS, but it’s gotten a lot more useful in the past year thanks to several recent upgrades.

Now tvOS 27 has introduced another improvement. Per Apple’s official release notes:

Individual app controls in Settings let you block users from launching specific apps.

This change is clearly intended for parents. 

Profiles for children can already limit the types of content they’ll see in the Apple TV app. That’s a useful feature, but it won’t keep your child from opening a different app with no such restrictions.

	

Now though, parents can open Settings and block certain apps from being launched at all when a child’s profile is active.

It’s a good step toward making profiles as full-featured as they deserve to be, and aligns with Apple’s recent focus in iOS 27 on upgrading parental controls.

On the subject of profile improvements, iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 will bring Apple’s profile system to iPhone and iPad for the first time. You can read about that change here.

Do you use profiles on your Apple TV? What new features do you hope get added? Let us know in the comments.

title: Apple Card adds new feature in iOS 27 that every card should have
snippet: iOS 27 brings a variety of new features to Apple Wallet, including one exclusive to Apple Card that I wish every card offered: a hub for all recurring transactions. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 brings a variety of new features to Apple Wallet, including one exclusive to Apple Card that I wish every card offered: a hub for all recurring transactions.

iOS 27 shows Apple Card recurring transactions in one place, making it easy to track subscriptions

Subscriptions are increasingly popular in the digital-centric world. As such, it can be easy to lose track of everything you’re subscribed to.

While plenty of apps and services offer to keep track of your subscriptions, giving third parties access to your financial info can spark privacy concerns. Fortunately, those solutions soon won’t be needed for Apple Card.

In iOS 27, the Wallet app offers a new feature for Apple Card users: a recurring transaction section.

When viewing your Apple Card in iOS 27, there’s a new ‘Recurring’ option inside the three-dot menu in the top-right corner.

Tapping this will show you a list of upcoming recurring transactions, and even lets you see them on a monthly calendar view.

I like to think I have a pretty good sense of all the things I’m subscribed to. But that takes effort. And Apple Card’s new feature makes tracking subscriptions pretty effortless.

I’m especially a fan of the calendar view, as it’s so nice getting to see at a glance exactly when each charge is expected to go through.

iOS 27 lists recurring transactions based on your Apple Card history, so it won’t always catch everything. The Wallet app has a disclaimer that states: “Dates and amounts shown are predicted based on your transaction history and may not be exact. Routine spending may incorrectly appear as recurring.”

If you do see an item that’s incorrectly marked as recurring, it’s easy to correct the error.

I really hope Apple Card inspires more credit cards and banks to copy iOS 27’s new feature. It feels like a no-brainer addition that every card should have.

Now I want to start moving all my subscriptions on to Apple Card.

title: The ultra-pocketable ‘Picco’ e-reader from Boox is now up for pre-order, $99
snippet: The tiny e-reader form factor is starting to make a big splash as the company behind some of the best Android e-readers announces its own version Boox calls the “Picco,” now available to pre-order. more…
fullText:
The tiny e-reader form factor is starting to make a big splash as the company behind some of the best Android e-readers announces its own version Boox calls the “Picco,” now available to pre-order.

The Boox Picco has really only been teased here and there. We got a preview at IFA 2026, but we didn’t get to dive in as much as we wanted. The unit was still pre-production and in need of various refinements. Still, Boox has been in this game for a while, so we expect a good experience.

Today, Boox announced that Picco is now available for pre-order on its website. It starts at $99, but the website lists it at $109 for those purchasing from the US warehouse.

The Picco’s black-and-white display comes in at just 3.97 inches, and even still, it offers a front light for day and night reading sessions. It weighs just 58 grams, and even though Boox doesn’t list the device’s thickness in the press release, our own hands-on would tell us the tiny e-reader is plenty thin.

	

It will still add a little bulk to your phone if you choose to attach it with magnets. While it isn’t magnetic by itself, the Boox Picco comes with a case that makes it possible. It’s one of the most demanded features for the tiny e-readers that have already been released, because it adds a second screen without the doomscrolling and eye strain.

Another great detail to point out during the pre-order phase is that the Boox Picco doesn’t run Android, which we covered previously. This means access to third-party apps from the Google Play Store isn’t available. Still, a simple experience will allow users to transfer files with a companion app if you don’t want to use the SD card slot to manually move ePUB files.

Boox’s adorable little Picco is expected to ship out around October for those who pre-order.

title: Motorola Signature 27 is a proper flagship with Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6
snippet: Alongside Qualcomm’s latest announcements, Motorola has officially shown off the Motorola Signature 27, a true flagship offering that’s set to launch before the end of this year. more…
fullText:
Alongside Qualcomm’s latest announcements, Motorola has officially shown off the Motorola Signature 27, a true flagship offering that’s set to launch before the end of this year.

Building on the Motorola Signature, a pseudo-flagship that launched earlier this year, the Signature 27 adopts a new naming scheme (based on the coming year), a wild-looking design, and a proper flagship spec sheet.

While its predecessor was based on Qualcomm’s step-down Snapdragon 8 Gen 5, the Motorola Signature 27 uses the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, a new chip that’s just as powerful as its mouthful of a name. It’s a big deal on Motorola’s part, as the brand hasn’t used any flagship chipsets in quite a while. The Motorola Razr Ultra (2025) used the Snapdragon 8 Elite, but its successor didn’t upgrade, and other devices in the company’s lineup, including the $1,900 Razr Fold, haven’t gone beyond the Snapdragon 8 Gen 5.

Qualcomm announces the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6

Motorola says to expect stronger on-device AI features with Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, as well as “responsive” gaming, faster download speeds over various networks, and improvements to the camera, too. There’s an “ArcticMesh” cooling system that combines a 40% larger vapor chamber with liquid metal, copper mesh, and “diamond-infused thermal gel.”

	

Motorola Signature 27 is promised 7 years of Android OS and security updates and has quite the look with its quad-camera setup on the back. That includes a 50MP Sony LYTIA 910 main sensor and 200MP periscope telephoto lens. The other two haven’t been confirmed just yet. The design itself brings back some Droid Razr vibes from over a decade ago. 

	

Signature 27 will come in “Coal Smoke” with a “Tactical Weave” finish, or “Capulet Green” with a “brushed textile-inspired finish.”

A firm release date hasn’t been announced, nor has Motorola spilled the beans on exact launch markets. The company says it will debut “worldwide” in 2026, and also confirmed a launch in North America in the “coming months.”

title: MacWhisper update brings real-time meeting transcripts, improved speaker recognition, more
snippet: My transcription tool of choice on the Mac, MacWhisper, got another major update today with real-time meeting transcripts, significantly improved speaker recognition, tighter integration with Apple Intelligence, and a new transcription model. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
My transcription tool of choice on the Mac, MacWhisper, got another major update today with real-time meeting transcripts, significantly improved speaker recognition, tighter integration with Apple Intelligence, and a new transcription model. Here are the details.

MacWhisper gets deeper Apple Intelligence integration

I’ve written in the past about how much I rely on MacWhisper, particularly as part of my podcast production workflow.

MacWhisper was one of the first AI-powered transcription tools for the Mac. Since indie developer Jordi Bruin launched it in 2023, it has been on a relentless streak of improvements and expanded support for new models, services, and workflows.

That has included everything from automatic meeting recording and speaker recognition to watched folders, system-wide dictation, local and cloud AI models, and integrations with services such as Notion, Zapier, Obsidian, and n8n.

Today, MacWhisper was updated to version 15.2, introducing an improved speaker recognition powered by NVIDIA’s Nemotron 3 Diarization model, which was announced just hours ago.

It supports up to 8 speakers and can also be used during live meetings in the new realtime meeting view!

Which brings us to another major addition in today’s update: real-time meeting transcriptions.

This feature had been sitting near the top of MacWhisper’s public roadmap for a while, and it is now here, allowing users to follow, refer back to, copy, or transfer a live transcript as the meeting unfolds.

You can keep the window above your other apps to follow along, and your recording and transcript are saved when the meeting ends.

When it comes to the actual transcription models, MacWhisper 15.2 adds Alibaba’s QWEN3-ASR transcription model with support for 22 languages, in addition to a tighter integration with Apple Intelligence, Siri, Spotlight, and Shortcuts on macOS 27.

Now, users running macOS (including in the EU) can search for transcripts system-wide, open them with Siri, pull their text into Shortcuts, and refer to the transcript currently on screen in Siri or Apple Intelligence requests.

Finally, MacWhisper 15.2 adds folders and subfolders for organizing transcripts and meetings, with support for dragging existing transcriptions into them from the sidebar.

Update 9/27:

Still rolling out (beta)

These are Messages features that Google announced or have been spotted in the wild by beta users.

Messages for web removing QR code pairing

Going forward, Messages for web users will have to use Google Account sign-in. As of late April, the QR code method is still available.

	

Learn more

Read receipts redesign

Read receipts are now placed in a circle at the bottom-right corner of message bubbles and images. You swipe left to see timestamps and the encryption lock, while you can swipe right to reply. This first started appearing in August of 2024, but is now seeing wide beta and stable availability.

Instead of a top toolbar, long-pressing on a message or image opens a floating menu as the background blurs. Another press lets you copy just a part of the chat. Previously, you had to copy the entire message.

The new Google Keep integration lets you quickly create and share notes inside chats. If you don’t see a contextual suggestion to “Create list,” open the ‘plus’ menu for a new “Keep Notes” tile.

This will slide up a sheet that shows your list of notes and the “Create a note” button. Upon selecting or starting a note, you’ll see a send button in the bottom-right corner. Afterward, there’s a live preview in the conversation thread.

Chat theme

	

Google Messages now lets you extensively customize conversations with a “Chat theme.” Replacing “Change colors” from 2024, you access this new option from the three-dot overflow menu. Be on the lookout for a red badge when this is rolled out for your phone. Themes will only appear on your device.

The Colors carousel themes message bubbles. There are nine options, with Dynamic Color being the first option and responding to the background of your chat.

The Wallpapers option lets you change the background of the conversation. In addition to uploading your own image, Google provides the following collections: Animals, Architecture, Black & White, Cityscapes, Landscapes, Macro, Space, Sunsets, and Textures.

title: Google Beam 3D meeting booths coming to co-working spaces
snippet: Google today announced the latest expansion of its 3D meeting booths, including a partnership that brings Google Beam to co-working spaces in the US. more…
fullText:
Google today announced the latest expansion of its 3D meeting booths, including a partnership that brings Google Beam to co-working spaces in the US.

Since last year’s launch and rename from Project Starline, Google Beam has only been available to large companies. Early partners include Bain & Company, Netflix, and Capital Group. Internally, Google has expanded Beam deployment for its employees.

Over an eight-week internal study, Google teams using Beam felt 50% more connected to one another, found it 33% easier to ensure their feedback was clearly understood, and saw a 21% drop in the need for follow-up meetings.

Google is now launching the first ever “Beam extended network.” Industrious is a “global operator of premium flexible workspaces worldwide.”

You will soon be able to visit locations in Atlanta, Chicago, New York City, and Palo Alto to book and use the HP Dimension unit, which supports Google Meet and Zoom. 

	

In piloting this year, Google found that distributed teams are using Beam for “manager check-ins, interviews, and client consultations.” Google Beam availability at Industrious locations starts this October. 

Meanwhile, Google is now shipping Beam units to customers in the US, Canada, UK, France, Germany, and Japan. This expansion is in partnership with 18 channel partners.
