title: Report: Apple working on new Vision Pro, with different form factors on the table
snippet: After the release of Vision Pro, everyone wanted to know how long it would be before the company could release a lighter version that isn’t so bulky on your face. For the longest time, we had been looking forward to a so-called Vision Air, codenamed N100. That project was shelved last year, though the company is working on a new project with similar aspirations, per Bloomberg. more…
fullText:
After the release of Vision Pro, everyone wanted to know how long it would be before the company could release a lighter version that isn’t so bulky on your face. For the longest time, we had been looking forward to a so-called Vision Air, codenamed N100. That project was shelved last year, though the company is working on a new project with similar aspirations, per Bloomberg.

Unlike the previous N100 project, it doesn’t seem the new project, N224, is necessarily targeted at being a lower cost offering. It could instead be a successor to the current M5-based Vision Pro model, though it might still come in at a lower price while offering the flagship experience.

This new version seems relatively early in the works, with Bloomberg reporting that it could arrive between late 2028 and early 2029. That said, it isn’t quite clear what exactly Apple will be going for. The company currently has four concepts in the works.

One of the concepts is similar to the recently unveiled Meta VR glasses, which offloads the compute and battery to an external puck. Given the fact that Vision Pro already has an external battery, offloading the compute doesn’t necessarily seem like a major hurdle, though you’d need better thermals and more efficient compute to pull that off.

On the other hand, some Apple executives reportedly don’t love the idea of an external puck, and “want the company to stick with something closer to an all-in-one design.”

Design wise, Apple might get a bit more experimental compared to the current Vision Pro, with the company supposedly considering other material choices. From the Power On newsletter:

One design in testing retains the basic egg-shaped form of the current Vision Pro, but Apple is actively exploring ways to reduce its weight by experimenting with plastic, titanium, other metals and various materials. The company has also continued to explore a standalone puck that combines the computing components and battery, similar to the approach used by Meta’s recent VR Glasses.

Wrap up

Time will tell what Apple will actually end up delivering. Given the A20 Pro chip being incredibly performant at its thermal envelope, it seems highly likely that in another 2 years, we could have an A-series chip capable of running visionOS at a higher capacity than the current M5, while not needing active cooling.

	

I do think Apple should go all in on the Meta VR glasses idea. Even at a higher price point, I think the form factor makes a ton of sense. Apple silicon, EyeSight, and visionOS will allow the product stand out.

What do you think of this new Vision Pro news? Are you a current Vision Pro owner, or are you still skeptical of the idea of headsets? Let us know in the comments.

title: Apple hit with $5.7 billion verdict over Taptic Engine patent infringement
snippet: Apple must pay $5.7 billion for infringing on patents held by Taction Technology, a US jury ruled on Friday. The patents relate to Apple’s Taptic Engine, which is the hardware Apple uses to provide haptic feedback for notifications, button presses, and other interactions. Taction first filed the lawsuit in 2021, alleging Apple had “infringed and continues to infringe, directly and indirectly” its patents. more…
fullText:
Apple must pay $5.7 billion for infringing on patents held by Taction Technology, a US jury ruled on Friday. The patents relate to Apple’s Taptic Engine, which is the hardware Apple uses to provide haptic feedback for notifications, button presses, and other interactions.

Taction first filed the lawsuit in 2021, alleging Apple had “infringed and continues to infringe, directly and indirectly” its patents.

As reported by CNBC, the lawsuit centered around two patents:

U.S. Patent No. 10,659,885

U.S. Patent No. 10,820,117

Both patents are focused on a “vibration module for applying vibrational tractions to a wearer’s skin.” Taction argued that Apple’s Taptic Engine infringes upon its patents, saying that Apple was “capitalizing on Taction’s innovation and success.”

Apple’s Taptic Engine first debuted as part of the Apple Watch in 2014 and came to the iPhone 6s and iPhone 6s Plus the following year, replacing the older vibration motor.

In a statement, an Apple spokesperson said:

“While we thank the jury for their consideration, we strongly disagree with today’s verdict and the damages awarded, which are entirely unsupported by the facts.

Apple’s Taptic Engine is fundamentally different from Taction’s technology, which Taction’s own testing of Apple’s products confirmed during trial. Apple does not use Taction’s technology, and we will appeal.”

Taction Technology is a California-based company that describes itself as being “obsessed by sound.” The company says that its “Transporter Technology powers the game-changing Corsair HS60 Haptic headphones, and will soon be powering other premium headphones from major manufacturers.”

In a statement to CNBC, Taction’s lead counsel said:

“We’re happy the jury found for Taction and vindicated its patent rights. Taction waited five and a half years for this case to get to trial, so it was a long time coming.”

You can read the original complaint for patent infringement filed by Taction here and Friday’s jury ruling here.

The Polaroid Mod is launching globally starting today for $169.99 through Polaroid's online store and will be available from other US retailers on October 6th. Two of the modes combine multiple exposures into one image using a simple process that invo … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
Andrew Liszewski

 

is a senior reporter who’s been covering and reviewing the latest gadgets and tech since 2006, but has loved all things electronic since he was a kid.

Polaroid announced a new instant camera that lets photographers get more creative and experimental with their shots than just changing the aperture or shutter speed. In addition to a Brightness dial on the front for adjusting exposure, the new Polaroid Mod has a dial around the lens for switching between four “creative shooting modes” with unique analog effects that are all captured in-camera. The Polaroid Mod is launching globally starting today for $169.99 through Polaroid’s online store and will be available from other US retailers on October 6th.

Two of the modes combine multiple exposures into one image using a simple process that involves capturing two separate exposures, one after the other, when prompted by the camera. Double Exposure layers two images atop each other to blend subjects or scenes together while Split Shot divides images into two halves using a rotating accessory that blocks half the lens at a time.

Light Painting uses a long exposure to capture light trails from a flashlight, sparkler, or other bright source while the camera is perched atop a stable tripod to keep other static elements in frame from becoming blurred. Motion Freeze is Polaroid’s name for the second curtain sync or rear curtain flash feature found in other cameras. A slower shutter speed is used to capture motion trails of a moving subject that’s combined with a sharp image of them captured by firing the Mod’s flash at the end of the exposure.

The Polaroid Mod works with Polaroid i-Type and 600 film stocks in color or black and white, and on a full charge of its 750mAh battery it can shoot up to 15 packs of film, which is up to 120 exposures. It uses a fixed focus two-lens system with a 103mm standard lens and a 95mm portrait lens that can be swapped as needed depending on the subject.

title: US Adults Have Tighter Holiday Shopping Budgets Amid Rising Tech Costs, CNET Finds
snippet: Can the average $808 holiday shopping budget squeeze in more pricey tech?
fullText:
Holiday shopping is expected to look much different this year with tighter budgets and higher prices. CNET’s annual holiday shopping survey found that close to three of every four holiday shoppers (73%) plan to buy tech this holiday season, and they expect to spend an average of $808 on tech products and services during that time. But is that enough, given the RAM shortage driving higher everyday costs?

CNET’s shopping team has been tracking price increases across tech since mid-2025, and CNET’s director of commerce content, Russell Holly, says even steep discounts aren’t lowering prices as much as before. But there’s a lot that goes into holiday shopping this year, including a smaller shopping budget and frustrations such as misleading discounts and inflated baseline prices. 

The holidays are fast approaching, and early holiday sales are coming up, like Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days on Oct. 6-7, and Walmart’s Deals & More sale on Oct. 5-11. So you’ll need to do some planning and know when to buy tech must-haves amid the shopping chaos. Here’s what US adults expect during the upcoming holiday shopping season and how to find deals without overspending

			

More from CNET

Key findings

Nearly one-third (32%) of US adults plan to start holiday shopping before November, and 27% plan to shop during sales. 

US adults plan to spend less on holiday shopping compared to last year. This year, holiday tech shoppers plan to spend an average of $808 on consumer tech products and services – that’s $123 less than last year’s holiday shopping average. 

Most shoppers (84%) expect purchasing frustrations like misleading discounts (43%), instant product sellouts (39%) and inflated baseline prices (35%).

US adults plan to buy toys and kitchen items more compared to tech items like headphones, phones, TVs and laptops.

Most US adults plan to shop early and spend less 

Most US adults aren’t waiting until the usual Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales in November to start holiday shopping. CNET found that close to one-third (32%) will start holiday shopping before November. Many have already started or plan to by October. By month, 27% of US adults plan to shop in November, while 18% plan to shop in October. And as the holidays inch closer, 11% say they will shop in December.

Cole Kan/CNET

Over a quarter of US adults (27%) plan to take advantage of savings events, like Amazon’s and Walmart’s upcoming holiday sales, while 18% of those shopping between October and November don’t plan to. The big question is whether or not the sales are worthwhile. Holly says it comes down to when you find a deal that’s worthwhile. 

“The best time to buy is the moment you see something you want on an actual discount, because increased prices can come at any time,” Holly said. 

Even if tech’s not high on your shopping list, the right deals may make you reconsider. 

CNET’s deals team spends hours making sure sales are legitimate — not just a fake price drop. And in the coming weeks, they’ll track deals on devices like laptops, headphones, wearable devices and smart home gadgets, plus alternatives to more costly tech, to help you determine what’s worth buying now or later.

You can also check an item’s price history to see if you’re getting the best deal by using price trackers like CamelCamelCamel and comparing prices across retailers before buying. But as Holly noted, if you want to upgrade your personal devices, don’t wait. Look for the best price you can find and buy it right away. Otherwise, prices may go up while you wait. 

US adults plan to spend $123 less than holiday shopping last year 

Last year, CNET found that US adults planned to spend an average of $931 on holiday shopping. This year, shoppers are planning to spend less. 

On average, they expect to spend $808 on holiday shopping. That’s $123 less than last year. Some generations plan to spend more, such as Millennials, who anticipate an average holiday shopping outlay of $1,074. Boomers will spend around half that amount — $582. 

Cole Kan/CNET

Higher everyday living costs could explain why holiday budgets are lower.

“Everything else being more expensive means less left over for gifts,” said Holly. “There’s very little indication that component prices are going to come back down anytime soon, so if you’re hoping for the kinds of prices you saw even two years ago, I would say you’re going to be waiting quite a while.”

Balancing holiday gifts and everyday basics on your usual income can be a lot to handle. Now’s the time to set holiday expectations, including a budget and a list of must-haves, along with more affordable options that still meet your needs. 

Then keep checking prices and deals from your trusted retailers and be prepared to buy when you spot good savings. Most importantly, try to avoid using credit cards and buy now, pay later plans that can lead to debt. The Federal Reserve’s recent rate hike will push borrowing costs higher, making debt more expensive through higher credit card and loan interest rates. 

Nearly 3 in 4 plan to buy tech this holiday season

CNET found that 73% of shoppers plan to buy tech products or services this season, but what most US adults plan to buy and how much they plan to spend may surprise you. 

Thirty percent of shoppers plan to purchase toys, and 25% plan to buy kitchen items, like air fryers and cookware. But shoppers don’t plan to buy as many personal electronics and home entertainment products. Only 20% plan to buy headphones or earbuds, and even fewer plan to buy video games for consoles (18%) or laptops and TVs (11%). More shocking is that only 13% plan to buy phones. We’ve seen prices increase across popular tech devices and brands due to the RAM shortage, which has led to low supply and high demand for memory chips. 

Cole Kan/CNET

Some of the latest releases cost way more than the average $808 most US adults plan to spend. For instance, the $2,000 iPhone Duo by itself costs even more than the average $1,704 that Millennials plan to spend on tech this holiday season. And less costly phones are still beyond holiday budgets, like the $1,200 iPhone 18 Pro Max, and even the iPhone 18 Pro is $1,200. Trade-in offers and sales can help lower that cost if you’re planning to upgrade, but shop around and compare deals before buying.

Increased prices may make you reconsider whether to stick with your current model or upgrade, but remember, you have options. 

“If the current laptop works well enough, upgrading can either be viewed as a luxury purchase for later or shifted to buying used or refurbished models to save extra,” Holly said. 

You may also consider a slightly older model of the device you’re looking for. It could still have all of the features you need, but cost less. Another money-saving option is to consider refurbished tech that’s in excellent or good condition from a certified refurbished retailer. You may still notice some price increases due to demand, but it could still cost less than the newest models.  

US adults are bracing for higher prices and fake deals

Most US shoppers (84%) expect the holiday shopping season to come with a few hurdles this year. Forty-three percent are concerned about deceptive pricing practices, such as retailers raising original prices before discounting them for a sale. Others are concerned about deals selling out immediately because of low stock or automated buying bots (39%). 

Take Nintendo’s Zelda Switch 2 to commemorate the Legend of Zelda’s 40th anniversary. It costs $520, and preorders are sold out. But earlier this year, Nintendo announced a price increase for the regular Switch 2, which would start at $500, up $50 since its launch. So Zelda and Nintendo fans are juggling limited availability and higher prices for one item. 

There’s not much you can do about preorders selling out or limited stock of an item, but it’s best to have a backup plan. Consider other retailers or device options that you’ll still be satisfied with — like a Nintendo Switch 2 and the digital download of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time when it’s released.

But if you’re more worried about fake deals or sales being a money grab by retailers, Holly said that historically, there have been some great sales ahead of the holidays. It’s still best to do your research before buying to make sure you’re getting a deal by comparing retailer prices before and after announced sales and using price tracking tools, like CamelCamelCamel. Heads up that many retailers, like Amazon, have flash sales with specific times of deeper discounts, and you’ll need to act fast, so it’s best to plan your holiday shopping now.

“The best thing anyone can do ahead of a shopping event is prepare,” said Holly. “Find your favorite price tracker tool before the event starts, have a general idea of what you’re looking to buy and be sure to keep an eye out for bigger discounts when you bundle things together.”

Methodology

CNET commissioned YouGov Plc to conduct the survey. All figures, unless otherwise stated, are from YouGov Plc. The total sample size was 2,615 adults, of whom 1,552 were interested in purchasing consumer tech products or services this winter holiday season. Fieldwork was undertaken Sept. 3-6, 2026.  The survey was carried out online. The figures have been weighted and are representative of all US adults (aged 18 and older).

title: SNL Skewers Anthropic CEO: ‘I Urge You to Urge Me to Stop’
snippet: Jane Wickline plays a sweaty, Gollum-esque Dario Amodei in this sharp satire.
fullText:
If AI executives and employees really think artificial intelligence has a chance to kill us all, why are they still trying to make AI more powerful? According to a Saturday Night Live skit that aired this weekend, they want regular people like us to stop them. 

Thanks a lot for that responsibility. We’ll get right on that.

In the Weekend Update skit, cast member Jane Wickline plays a desperately nervous Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, referencing a recent unnerving interview he gave to CNN’s Anderson Cooper, in which the tech leader refuses to say that AI won’t destroy humanity. Amodei’s recent essay, We Must Pace the Frontier, published amid a surge in doomsday talk of human extinction, urged tech companies like his own to slow AI development.

			

More from CNET

“I want to assure you that, if we can pressure lawmakers to create guardrails, we will be able to stop me,” Wickline’s Amodei says in the skit.

When Weekend Update anchor Michael Che asked Amodei to explain how the company isn’t going to kill us, the stuttering fictional Amodei responds: “That’s a really hard question.”

Amodei’s character then engages in a disturbing dialogue with himself, using the voices of Sméagol and Gollum from The Lord of the Rings (Sméagol being the lingering memory of Gollum’s human self, and Gollum being the monstrous, single-minded, bent-on-destruction slave to the One Ring). 

He finally blurts out, “AI is the devil, and I its maker.”

SNL’s Amodei goes on to claim that he and the other AI executives, including OpenAI’s Sam Altman, “do not condone what we are doing.”

After a failed analogy about whether Che would drink milk that might make his life easier but might also kill him (he would not), Amodei announces that “AI is not a weapon. It’s a tool. A tool for building weapons. And I urge you to urge me to stop.”

The spoof was intended to capture the anxieties around the dangers of rogue AI. The sketch sparked discussion across social media, among people in the tech industry as well as SNL viewers.

“We will be rewatching this in our final days sometime in the next 10 years,”  one person wrote when SNL shared the video to YouTube.

Another wrote: “AI will replace us all, but at least we’ll always have Weekend Update to explain why it’s our fault.”

A representative for Anthropic didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

title: Microsoft quietly ending ‘Copilot+ PC’ branding for Windows laptops
snippet: After a couple of years of relentlessly pushing it, Microsoft is seemingly ending its Copilot+ PC branding for Windows laptops. more…
fullText:
After a couple of years of relentlessly pushing it, Microsoft is seemingly ending its Copilot+ PC branding for Windows laptops.

Windows Central spoke with executives from Microsoft and Qualcomm about the lack of Copilot+ PC branding on the latest Surface machines. While it’s not been said explicitly, Surface CVP Brett Ostrum all-but-confirmed the end of that branding by saying:

…these are not called Copilot+ PCs. They do meet all the requirements of our previous bar for what Copilot+ devices are. We still lean into the narrative around AI on the edge and being able to have a hybrid solution out there.

	

Copilot+ PC branding was generally used to identify a laptop that met certain hardware requirements around AI features, particularly the NPU, which virtually every mid-high-end laptop already supports. Windows Central further points out that Nvidia’s RTX Spark push has been absent of any mention of Copilot+ PC branding.

Microsoft started using this branding back in 2024, but when the flagship feature of the Copilot+ PC, Recall, was met with backlash, the branding became little more than a hardware checkbox that consumers didn’t fully understand. 

	

The only big question left – does this mean the Copilot Key is going away?

title: AirPods just got a long-requested feature in new software update
snippet: While it was overshadowed by release of iOS 27, Apple also released a new software update for AirPods this month. The update brings a long-requested feature to supported AirPods models: custom EQ. more…
fullText:
While it was overshadowed by release of iOS 27, Apple also released a new software update for AirPods this month. The update brings a long-requested feature to supported AirPods models: custom EQ.

AirPods software details

The latest AirPods firmware build number is 9A350 for AirPods 5 and 9A348 for the other models below. The update is available for the following AirPods models:

AirPods Pro 3

AirPods 4

AirPods 4 with Active Noise Cancellation 

AirPods 5

AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case

AirPods Pro 2 (Lightning and USB-C)

AirPods Max 2

Apple says that AirPods firmware updates are automatically installed while your AirPods are charging and within Bluetooth range of your iPhone, iPad, or Mac that’s connected to WiFi. You can check the firmware version of your AirPods in the Settings app on iPhone. 

Custom EQ comes to AirPods

Once you install the AirPods firmware update, you’ll see a long-awaited new feature in the Settings app: custom EQ.

You now have more control over how your AirPods sound thanks to the new custom EQ controls. In the Settings app, you can adjust the lows, mids, and highs of your AirPods sound.

“AirPods are designed and engineered by Apple to faithfully represent music, TV shows and movies, and calls,” Apple explains. “If you prefer a different sound profile, you can customize how AirPods represent any audio played.”

While adjusting the custom EQ settings, you can play a song from Apple Music right in the Settings app to hear the adjustments in real time.

This isn’t the most advanced equalizer feature out there. It’s a basic, three-band system. Still, it’s a long-awaited AirPods feature that Apple has finally given users—even if most will likely stick with the default levels.

You can find the new custom EQ feature in the AirPods section of the Settings app under the “Audio and Routing” menu. The feature is available on all AirPods with an H2 chip, including AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods 4, and AirPods Max 2.

Other iOS 27 features for AirPods

Here are the other new AirPods features for iOS 27:

Settings app redesign: In iOS 27, Apple has redesigned the AirPods interface in the Settings app. The controls have been reorganized, with separate menus for Hearing Health, Find My, Live Translation, and more.

Adaptive Audio slider: In the Settings app, you now have a slider to further fine-tune Adaptive Audio mode.

GymKit: While GymKit has been around for years, it’s always required an Apple Watch. As my colleague Zac explains, iOS 27 brings the full GymKit experience to iPhone and AirPods Pro 3.

Precision Finding: You can now use Precision Finding in the Find My app on Apple Watch to locate AirPods Pro 3.

Siri AI: When paired to a compatible iPhone, AirPods can interact with Siri AI.

Wrap up

title: Android Auto rolls out game support, no longer in beta
snippet: Google is graduating game support on Android Auto from a limited beta to broad availability, allowing developers to bring games to your car’s display. more…
fullText:
Google is graduating game support on Android Auto from a limited beta to broad availability, allowing developers to bring games to your car’s display.

First available last year, games in Android Auto and Android Automotive bring a bit of interactive fun to the car’s display. While there’s no direct integration with things like the car’s steering wheel, it’s a nice way to add something fun to the biggest screen in your vehicle for times you might be stuck on the side of the road, waiting on an EV to charge, or other times where the vehicle is not moving.

Around 30 games are available on Android Auto today, but that list is likely to start expanding soon.

Google announced this week that game support on Android Auto is no longer in beta, meaning that game support is open to all developers rather than requiring specific approval from Google. 

	

Google says:

Bringing your game to cars lets you reach users in their vehicles during natural downtime, such as while waiting at a charging station or for a curbside order pickup. Today’s milestone means that we’re opening up access so developers can now publish games to the open testing and production tracks on Google Play. In this post, we’ll cover how to adapt your existing Android game for the car screen, focusing on key technical requirements and publishing criteria.

Android games must declare support for Android Auto and Android Automotive OS – they’re separate declarations behind the scenes, and there are many more games that support Android Automotive without Android Auto support as it stands today.

Games on Android Auto should be able to adapt to different display sizes and need to recognize when a vehicle is parked or not – games can only be played if the vehicle is parked. Games can also support controllers on Android Auto and Android Automotive. 

Google’s full documentation on what developers need to do can be found here.

Apple debuted the all-new AirPods 5 this month, and they bring ANC to lower prices than ever before. If you’re shopping for AirPods, however, there are still several reasons you might want to opt for the more expensive AirPods Pro 3.

Buy AirPods Pro $234 (Reg. $249)

Buy AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case $149

Different design

AirPods are one of Apple’s most personal products. The fit can vary dramatically between different people depending on the size of their ears. AirPods 5 offer an open-ear design, so they rest on the inside of your ear. AirPods Pro, meanwhile, offer a more traditional in-ear design with ear tips.

Personally, I find AirPods Pro to be more comfortable than AirPods 5. They’re also more secure for me, so I’m less worried they’ll fall out of my ears.

Heart rate monitoring

One of the key differentiators between AirPods Pro 3 and AirPods 5 is that AirPods Pro 3 offer built-in heart rate monitoring capabilities. During a workout, AirPods Pro can measure your heart rate to provide additional fitness metrics.

If you wear an Apple Watch, AirPods Pro 3 work along with your Apple Watch to ensure you get the most accurate data possible. Apple’s algorithms monitor the data from AirPods Pro and Apple Watch, and factor in the type of workout you’re doing, to use the most consistent data possible. For example, if you’re lifting weights and the Apple Watch ends up at an awkward angle on your wrist, AirPods Pro 3 will step in to provide more accurate data.

Furthermore, in iOS 27, Apple brought GymKit to the iPhone, so you can use iPhone and AirPods to get an Apple Watch-style experience … but without wearing a watch. Learn more about this change in Zac’s full coverage.

Hearing Aid

AirPods Pro 3 offer a range of hearing health features that aren’t available on AirPods 5. This includes:

Hearing Test

Hearing Aid

Hearing Protection

With the Hearing Test feature, you can take a 5-minute test to identify if you have hearing loss. Apple’s Hearing Aid feature, meanwhile, is a clinical-grade hearing aid that uses the results of your test to craft a sound profile for your needs. Finally, Hearing Protection, can help prevent exposure to loud environmental noise.

Wrap up

There are other reasons to choose AirPods Pro over AirPods 5, including longer battery life, even better ANC, and a more capable charging case. The difference in ANC, in particular, is notable: Apple says AirPods Pro 3 offer 3x more Active Noise Cancellation than AirPods 5.

title: Android’s Digital Wellbeing appears to be ditching ‘Heads up’ walking alerts
snippet: Google appears to be pulling the plug on a Digital Wellbeing feature called “Heads up” which is designed to help you stay off of your phone for extended periods of time while walking. more…
fullText:
Google appears to be pulling the plug on a Digital Wellbeing feature called “Heads up” which is designed to help you stay off of your phone for extended periods of time while walking.

Introduced in 2021, “Heads up” was designed to help you curb your smartphone use while walking since, when looking at your phone, you’re probably not fully aware of your surroundings. Alerts such as “Look ahead” and “Watch your step” would appear if you were using your phone while walking for a certain length of time.

Now, Google seems to be removing it.

In the Digital Wellbeing v1.48.975819457.beta release, the folks over at Android Authority noticed strings regarding “Heads up deprecation.” Google explicitly says:

	

Walking detection is going away soon

There’s no word on why it’s being removed, though it’s certainly odd given that the feature at least appears to run on device. It’s easy to guess that the feature was probably underused, being an opt-in feature, but it’s strange seeing as there’s no obvious burden to just leaving it in place. 

As it stands, the feature is still active and, with the altered strings only in the beta track, it’s probably not going away imminently, but we’ll have to wait and see what other details come to light as the removal nears.

snippet: The Android Dev Summit is returning in 2026 after Google’s last focused developer conference in 2022. Additionally, the agenda comes with a mention of Android 18. more…
fullText:
The Android Dev Summit is returning in 2026 after Google’s last focused developer conference in 2022. Additionally, the agenda comes with a mention of Android 18.

The last Android Dev Summit was in 2022. The developer-focused event is now back with two days of programming at Google’s headquarters in Mountain View, as well as a satellite “Extended” event in London.

There will be a “keynote with Android leadership on the latest features and updates.” There are four conference tracks: AI experiences, Android XR, Apps foundation, and Tools and performance. 

Meanwhile, we get our first mention of Android 18, including how there will be “powerful new graphics features.”

	

“Elevate your apps with the latest graphics features in Jetpack Compose and Android 18” is a particularly interesting session:

Ready to take your Android UI from “it works” to “it’s a work of art”? 

	

Join us for a tour of the latest graphics capabilities in Jetpack Compose. We’ll show you how to build new visual effects, from delightful mesh gradients to progressive blurs, and using the powerful new graphics features in Android 18. We will also show you how to improve the performance of your graphics features, without sacrificing battery life or frame rates.

It will be interesting to see if Android 18 is announced at or just before the conference. Android no longer has developer previews in light of the Canary channel. But for reference, Android 16 testing began in November. Any sort of Android 18 preview in October would be very early.

Android XR and AI are big focuses, with notable sessions about how to:

Connect your apps to Gemini, Search and the Android intelligence system: “Explore how to connect your applications seamlessly to Gemini, Search and the Android intelligence system.”

title: Anker’s 25W MagSafe 3-in-1 packs active cooling in a travel-sized design [Hands-on]
snippet: If you’re rocking an iPhone 16 or newer, you might be interested in a Qi2.2 charger to take full advantage of the 25W MagSafe charging speeds that your phone can support. Anker’s new 25W Prime MagSafe 3-in-1 is one of many great options, and it comes in an excellent portable design. more…
fullText:
If you’re rocking an iPhone 16 or newer, you might be interested in a Qi2.2 charger to take full advantage of the 25W MagSafe charging speeds that your phone can support. Anker’s new 25W Prime MagSafe 3-in-1 is one of many great options, and it comes in an excellent portable design.

Impressions

The big trend of the latter half of 2025 was bringing 25W Qi2.2 to every single wireless charging accessory possible, and that’s continued through 2026. Anker is kicking things off with a new portable MagSafe 3-in-1 that packs 25W Qi2.2 support into a very portable design.

With 25W of wireless charging, active cooling is practically a necessity. Nearly every 25W charger on the market integrates it, and the new Anker foldable 3-in-1 is no exception.

In the box, you get a 45W charge brick and USB-C cable – providing ample power to charge your iPhone, AirPods, and Apple Watch all at once. With this stand, you can charge an iPhone 18 Pro to 50% in just 27 minutes.

Remember MagSafe Duo? If you were someone who really enjoyed that product before Apple killed it off, you’ll likely enjoy this one. It has extremely similar portability characteristics, but comes with two key benefits: it can serve as a stand, and it can charge three devices at once instead of two.

One neat (though totally unnecessary) feature on this charger is that the Apple Watch charger is spring-loaded. It does fold inwards while you have the charger compacted, but when you’re ready to unfold everything, you just need to press downward on it and it springs outward. I thought that was pretty neat, and helps justify the premium price tag that this product demands.

Wrap up

All in all, if you want a nice MagSafe 3-in-1 charger that can easily work for travel, this new Anker offering is a great choice. Since it includes active cooling, it actually charges your iPhone rather quickly without any of the overheating or other negative side affects that wireless charging can sometimes have.

title: iPhone 18 Pro one week later: Zero compromises
snippet: I’ve been using iPhone 18 Pro for the past week after a full year as an iPhone Air user. And while there are advantages with each model, my main takeaway about iPhone 18 Pro so far is that it has zero compromises. Here’s what I mean. more…
fullText:
I’ve been using iPhone 18 Pro for the past week after a full year as an iPhone Air user. And while there are advantages with each model, my main takeaway about iPhone 18 Pro so far is that it has zero compromises. Here’s what I mean.

iPhone 18 Pro: The best camera system, battery life, and performance

If you want to buy a new iPhone, chances are the iPhone 18 Pro is a strong contender.

I’ve had mine for a week now, a Burgundy model that replaced my iPhone Air. And despite loving the Air a lot, it’s hard to match Apple’s no-compromise approach to the iPhone 18 Pro.

Cameras are better and far more versatile on iPhone 18 Pro compared to the Air. Telephoto and Ultra Wide lenses are great for specific use cases, but even the Main camera is better on iPhone 18 Pro.

Battery life is similarly impressive. I generally found the iPhone Air’s battery good enough for everyday use, and only needed to charge mid-day occasionally. But with iPhone 18 Pro I don’t even have to think about battery.

Performance is fantastic too. The A20 Pro chip makes everything on the iPhone feel fast, and I’ve even noticed a more responsive Siri AI. Thanks to the vapor chamber, I haven’t had any issues of overheating either, which the Air sometimes struggled with.

I’m not a pro photographer, and if you want battery tests or performance benchmarks, my colleague Chance’s iPhone 18 Pro review has you covered. But after a week with iPhone 18 Pro, that word “best” keeps coming back to me.

iPhone 18 Pro (and Pro Max) pack the absolute best camera system Apple makes, have the best battery life, and perform better than any other models. I’ve even noticed smaller improvements: the better built-in speakers and Dynamic Island upgrades are highlights.

There are measurable differences in all these areas, but I also appreciate just knowing my iPhone has the “best” Apple offers in key areas that matter most. There’s no wondering: would these pictures of my family look better if I used a different iPhone? Would this slowdown have happened?

All the positives of iPhone 18 Pro aside though, I’ll admit that I’m still very intrigued by the forthcoming iPhone Duo.

iPhone Duo, like iPhone Air, will be compromised but so compelling

The iPhone Air and iPhone Duo share a lot in common. Besides having similar design traits, they also both have shortcomings.

Like my iPhone Air, the iPhone Duo will have a worse camera system than iPhone 18 Pro. Battery might be comparable but definitely worse than the Pro Max, and I suspect sustained performance will lag a bit too. iPhone Duo will also lack Face ID and the Action button.

Yet despite these compromises, I’m very excited to get my hands on the device. 

That’s because it offers a lot of compelling innovations not found in iPhone 18 Pro. The foldable form factor represents arguably the biggest iPhone hardware change ever.

I’ve been enjoying my iPhone 18 Pro a lot. But guess what happened when I picked up the iPhone Air the other day?

I instantly said, “Wow.”

Here’s my iPhone 18 Pro Max review:

Do not buy an iPhone Air unless you want to immediately return every other phone forever.

— Ben Thompson (@benthompson) September 21, 2026

The Air’s thinness had become the norm for me after a year of use. But several days into using iPhone 18 Pro, I was able to find fresh appreciation for how futuristic the Air feels. And I suspect iPhone Duo will evoke similar feelings—not just for its design, but its utility too.

	

I’m excited to have an iPad-like experience with the iPhone that fits in my pocket. That’s true despite being admittedly torn about the downsides the Duo will bring.

The days of Apple offering a single “best” iPhone are gone. If you want a model with zero compromises, iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max seem fantastic. But for something more futuristic and unique, I still can’t wait to try iPhone Duo.

title: Emmy wins and recent premieres help Apple TV reach highest weekly viewership ever
snippet: Deadline reports that Apple TV recently recorded its biggest week ever for viewership, fueled by its 29 Emmy wins and recent releases such as Ted Lasso and Mayday. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Deadline reports that Apple TV recently recorded its biggest week ever for viewership, fueled by its 29 Emmy wins and recent releases such as Ted Lasso and Mayday. Here are the details.

Apple TV sees record viewership following the Emmys

A few weeks ago, Apple TV broke its own record with a total of 29 Emmy wins, 14 of which went to surprise hit Widow’s Bay.

Around the same time, Apple TV subscribers also got the return of Slow Horses, alongside recent releases including the Ryan Reynolds and Kenneth Branagh-led Mayday and the much-anticipated fourth season of Ted Lasso.

According to Deadline, this perfect storm helped Apple TV record its “highest weekly viewership ever for the week of Sept. 14, rising by +67% year-over-year.”

From Deadline:

Released straight-to-streaming on Sept. 4, Mayday has become Apple TV’s biggest film debut on the platform to date over its first 18 days, the company said. In the U.S., Mayday opened at No. 1 in Luminate’s Sept. 4-10 weekly rankings with 8.7M views. It remained strong in Week 2, placing at No.2.

The site also notes that, according to Apple TV, Widow’s Bay saw a whopping 280% week-over-week increase in viewership during the week after the Emmys, where it took home 14 awards, including Outstanding Comedy Series.

Apple TV noted that the increase was particularly notable in “the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Brazil, Mexico, Germany, India, Poland, and Spain,” says Deadline.

The company added that Pluribus saw a similar effect following its six Emmy wins, including Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series for Rhea Seehorn. The series “experienced a 200% surge in viewership week-over-week following the ceremony,” according to Apple.

Finally, Deadline notes that while the Emmys and recent premieres certainly helped drive the gains, Apple’s recent iCloud+ expansion may also have played a role.

Earlier this month, Apple began including Apple TV with iCloud+ at no extra charge in more than 100 countries, a rollout that also brought the streaming service to 59 new markets for the first time, expanding its total reach to 170 countries.

title: Google says Gemini 4 release is coming ‘as soon as possible’
snippet: As its rivals continue to iterate quickly, Google has confirmed that its Gemini 4 flagship AI model is nearing release and that it is coming “as soon as possible.” more…
fullText:
As its rivals continue to iterate quickly, Google has confirmed that its Gemini 4 flagship AI model is nearing release and that it is coming “as soon as possible.”

Google DeepMind chief Koray Kavukcuoglu confirmed to The Information at the publication’s AI Agenda Live Summit this week that its next flagship Gemini model, Gemini 4, has entered “post-training,” a phase in which the model’s behavior is refined ahead of a public release. This includes safety testing and implementing guardrails, with internal testing underway using Gemini 4 to power Antigravity.

In other words, Google is getting closer to the release of Gemini 4.

Kavukcuoglu explained:

	

Our intention is to, like—as soon as possible—to release an early post-training output because we see the results and we are excited… [to] continue the fast-paced iterations.

He adds that he hopes the model will be released “much earlier” than the end of 2026, but a specific timeline was not shared.

	

The update comes just days after Anthropic and OpenAI have both launched major updates to their respective flagship AI models in recent weeks. Responding to the idea that Google has “fallen behind,” Kavukcuoglu said that “I have the utmost trust in the team” and that “in my mind, it’s a certainty that we are always gonna be at the frontier.”

Google’s last major flagship model release was in November 2025 with Gemini 3 Pro, followed by Gemini 3.1 Pro in February 2026. There have been several updates to Flash and other models in the time since, most recently with Gemini 3.8 Flash. Google teased Gemini 3.5 Pro over the Summer, but never ended up releasing the model, and this week’s conversation with The Information sheds no light on whether or not that model will be released – Kavukcuoglu said that Google “took a little bit of a step back” to focus on its Flash models instead, but that the current focus is on releasing Gemini 4.

Speaking on AGI, a common conversation around other major AI model updates, Kavukcuoglu says that “the conversation is more about are we able to build intelligent agents that we can trust.”

fullText:
This week saw the debut of Qualcomm’s latest Snapdragon chips and, with it, the usual onslaught of Tensor hate around Google’s Pixel phones. Personally, I don’t care about those, but new launches around Qualcomm’s event have shown off a lot of other specs I’d much rather see Pixel adopt.

9to5Google Weekender by Ben Schoon is a part of our free newsletter that also includes ‘Inbox,’ a twice-weekly roundup of key stories from around the web by Daniel Bader. Sign up here to get Weekender delivered to your inbox every Sunday along with ‘Inbox’ on Tuesday and Thursday. You can find past issues here.

Google’s Tensor chip in Pixel phones has been a hot-button issue for enthusiasts for the entire time Google has been working on the project. And, I get it. Tensor is objectively not as powerful as a flagship Snapdragon or MediaTek chip and, with Pixel phones getting more and more expensive, that’s hard to accept. Google has solved many of the biggest deficiencies, leading to fairly wide acceptance from the “average Joe” customer base that Google is aiming for in the first place, but every year the same conversation comes back up with a new Snapdragon chip – “I wish that was in my Pixel.”

Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 family – I’m choosing to not put “Extreme” into that word salad here – looks incredible, and MediaTek’s new Dimensity 9600 Pro is also going to be solid. It’s totally okay to be annoyed that Pixels don’t get the same raw horsepower.

	

But, for me at least, it’s everything else that I wish Google would get a bit more on board with.

This week’s new chip launches also saw the announcement of new phones using those chips and, man, it’s wild how much faster these other brands are progressing compared to market staples like Pixel and Galaxy. The Xiaomi 18 Pro and Oppo Find X10 look insane. 

Xiaomi 18 Pro series goes official with ‘privacy screen,’ 8,500 mAh battery, and Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6

Oppo Find X10 series goes official with triple 200MP cameras, 8,000 mAh battery

8,000+ mAh batteries, a plethora of 200MP cameras, that’s the sort of stuff I wish I was getting on my Pixel. Forget horsepower, give me battery life and camera sensors that look good even before the power of computational photography steps in. The Oppo Find X9 Ultra was a big wake-up for me in that regard, as it was the first phone in quite a while that made me want to ditch the Pixel from my phone lineup (and I’m sure our Inbox author Daniel Bader is greatly enjoying it after prying it from my “Techtember”-ed fingers).

Google, if you’re listening, the rest of the Android world is frankly killing it on the hardware front right now. The software is still so-so in my book, but the practical wins that come from these all-out builds are too great to ignore. So, Pixel 12 maybe? Thanks.

Googlebook is here – what do you think?

title: Gemini fully replaces Google Assistant on Android
snippet: At the start of September, the Google Assistant deprecation on mobile got underway. It now looks to be widely rolling out. more…
fullText:
At the start of September, the Google Assistant deprecation on mobile got underway. It now looks to be widely rolling out.

Google has been moving Assistant users to Gemini over the past few weeks. This deprecation was originally set for 2025 and later extended to 2026. In early August, Google announced the final timeline.

Gemini is now the “voice assistant experience on Android” when you long-press the power button or swipe from the corners.

title: Apple and Amazon face renewed UK antitrust lawsuit
snippet: A UK tribunal has allowed part of a renewed antitrust lawsuit against Apple and Amazon to move forward, over allegations that the companies restricted competition for Apple and Beats products sold on Amazon. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
A UK tribunal has allowed part of a renewed antitrust lawsuit against Apple and Amazon to move forward, over allegations that the companies restricted competition for Apple and Beats products sold on Amazon. Here are the details.

A bit of context

Back in 2023, Apple and Amazon were hit with a proposed UK class action over a 2018 agreement that allegedly restricted which third-party sellers could offer Apple and Beats products through Amazon’s marketplace, reducing competition and, as a result, driving up prices for consumers.

It is worth noting that the UK was not the only market where the agreement drew scrutiny. Apple and Amazon have faced antitrust investigations and legal challenges over similar reseller restrictions in countries including Italy, Spain, Germany, and the United States.

In the British lawsuit, a class representative led by consumer law academic Christine Riefa accused the companies of reducing competition and driving up prices for consumers buying Apple and Beats products in the UK.

Last year, however, Britain’s Competition Appeal Tribunal refused to certify the case, citing concerns about how the lawsuit was being financed and about Riefa’s ability to independently protect the interests of the class.

The court took particular issue with the fact that, under the funding agreement, Asertis (which was financing the litigation in exchange for a success fee) could potentially have been paid out of any damages award before consumers received anything. The tribunal said the arrangement could even have resulted in the class receiving no damages at all.

From the decision:

“Our overall impression was that Prof Riefa was extremely reliant on her legal

advisers. We were not convinced that she had properly understood the

arrangements into which the PCR had entered on behalf of the Proposed Class

Members, and we were concerned about her ability to protect the interests of

the class robustly and independently.”

And

“Our key concern in this case is that Prof Riefa has not demonstrated sufficient

independence or robustness so as to act fairly and adequately in the interests of

the class.”

In its conclusion, the tribunal said a class representative cannot be “merely a figurehead” for proceedings being conducted by their lawyers, and that they should “act as the independent advocate for the class.”

The claim was later refiled by a new proposed class representative, Justin Le Patourel, which brings us to today.

UK tribunal allows part of lawsuit to proceed

As reported by Reuters, Britain’s Competition Appeal Tribunal today allowed part of the refiled lawsuit to proceed, while narrowing the case to claims involving Apple products purchased through Amazon’s marketplace.

From Reuters:

The tribunal allowed claims ​relating to Apple products bought through Amazon’s marketplace to proceed, but rejected ⁠one covering those bought directly from Apple and other retailers.

And

Judge Kelyn Bacon said claims relating to Amazon marketplace purchases were “plausible, credible ‌and ⁠grounded in the facts”, but rejected wider claims relating to other retailers because they rested on a “complex and speculative theory of harm”.

Reuters says the portion of the lawsuit now allowed to proceed could be worth between £289 million and £306 million, including interest.

Commenting on the decision, Apple told Reuters that its agreement with Amazon was intended to curb the sale of counterfeit products, and maintained that it “strongly” disagrees with the lawsuit.

Amazon, in turn, said it is confident the remaining claim will prove to be “without merit” as the legal process moves forward.

Finally, Reuters says a spokesperson for Le Patourel “welcomed the ruling, but said it was disappointing ​that parts ⁠of the claim were not certified.”

title: Apple says software update to fix iPhone 18 Pro rebooting bug is coming next week
snippet: On Monday, we reported on an issue where iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max users were seeing their phone freeze and reboot following a failed Face ID attempt. To us, it appeared to be a software glitch rather than an inherent hardware fault. Apple has now confirmed to 9to5Mac that a software update to address this problem is in the works, and should be available early next week. more…
fullText:
On Monday, we reported on an issue where iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max users were seeing their phone freeze and reboot following a failed Face ID attempt. To us, it appeared to be a software glitch rather than an inherent hardware fault.

Apple has now confirmed to 9to5Mac that a software update to address this problem is in the works, and should be available early next week.

Although the bug did not seemingly affect all users, it was reasonably widespread based on social media and 9to5Mac reader reports. 

At the time, we reproduced the problem on an iPhone 18 Pro device by obscuring our face with our hand as we attempted a Face ID authentication to access the Passwords app. The phone simply stops responding to touch input, and hard reboots after a few seconds. You could then find a panic log in the iPhone Analytics section of the Settings app.

iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max feature a redesigned Face ID sensor system, where the Infrared camera has moved behind the under the screen near where the clock is rendered in the status bar, resulting in a 25% smaller visible Dynamic Island. 

As we reported earlier in the week, some customers had already attempted to resolve the rebooting problem by swapping their phone with a new device at Apple, thinking it was a hardware fault. To reiterate, this is not necessary with a software fix now confirmed to be on the way. 

On a somewhat related note, Apple also just released watchOS 27.0.1 to fix a random restart issue with Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4.

title: Bose launched wired, yes, wired, earbuds with ANC for $99
snippet: The new Bose Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds connect via USB-C and work with almost any device. more…
fullText:
The new Bose Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds connect via USB-C and work with almost any device.

Bose wants to get back to basics, it seems – it just launched a new pair of wired earbuds with ANC, citing a rise in wired listening popularity. The earbuds connect to any USB-C device, using an internal, proprietary DSP to ensure they work in just about any USB-C port. With any source input, the earbuds output a fixed 24bit signal.

Bose is well-known for its Quiet Comfort lineup in recent years, but it didn’t start there. Still, the company can be considered one of the main players responsible for quality ANC in wireless headphones. After all, the QC35’s became the go-to travel option for some time.

This release, however, has literal strings attached. It needs USB-C to operate, not a 3.5mm output as most wired enthusiasts prefer at a minimum. That means you wouldn’t be able to use your own DAC/amp setup.

	

Even still, Bose’s Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds will be a good option for those who need ANC without the battery anxiety. Bose says the earbuds have two microphones on each bud to power active noise cancellation. Quiet Mode blocks most noise out, and Aware Mode acts as a transparency setting. ANC can also be disabled.

The new wired Bose earbuds are available to pre-order starting today for $99 in Black and White Smoke. Bose says the buds will begin shipping on October 15 for those who order from the official website and Best Buy.

title: Google confirms Photos bug that prevents editing and deleting, fix coming ‘ASAP’
snippet: Google Photos is undoubtedly the best way to manage your photo library on Android and beyond, but a recent bug has been stopping users from being able to commit even the most basic of tasks, including sharing, editing, and even delete images from their collection. Luckily, if you’ve found yourself dealing with these issues, Google has confirmed a fix is on the way. more…
fullText:
Google Photos is undoubtedly the best way to manage your photo library on Android and beyond, but a recent bug has been stopping users from being able to commit even the most basic of tasks, including sharing, editing, and even delete images from their collection. Luckily, if you’ve found yourself dealing with these issues, Google has confirmed a fix is on the way.

Various user reports on Reddit last week confirmed that a recent glitch has been preventing users from interacting with images after they’ve been edited. That includes sharing, adding to galleries, deleting, and re-editing photos, all from changes as simple as cropping an image. Luckily, Google confirmed in a statement with Android Authority — which reported on the app issues late last week — that a fix is being worked on, with the team working to roll it out “ASAP.”

The Google Photos team is working on rolling out a fix ASAP! […] For now, users can try these 2 workarounds: 1) Tap “Save as copy” when saving new edits, and 2) Visit photos.google.com to delete or share already-edited photos.

Until these changes are live, the company recommends either saving your image as a copy when creating new edits (to prevent locking up the original, sole copy of an image) or accessing the web version of Photos to share or delete as needed.

While I can’t say I’ve seen this bug on my own Pixel 11 Pro XL, it does appear that most of the affected users — or at least those reporting the issue online — are sporting the last few generations of Google’s Tensor-powered devices. If you’ve found yourself in that group, keep an eye on the Play Store for an update coming soon.

title: MacBook Pro redesign is coming, with three features we’ve waited years for
snippet: Apple has a big MacBook Pro redesign in the works (possibly called MacBook Ultra) that’s expected to launch in October. Here are three rumored new features that we’ve waited a long time for. more…
fullText:
Apple has a big MacBook Pro redesign in the works (possibly called MacBook Ultra) that’s expected to launch in October. Here are three rumored new features that we’ve waited a long time for.

#1: OLED display

It’s hard to overstate the value of display technology for a product that many users spend all day looking at. Yet for years, the Mac has lagged behind Apple’s other products in offering the most cutting-edge display tech.

OLED has been a mainstay on iPhone for years, and iPad Pro introduced a tandem OLED in 2024 that many Mac users pined for. Now with the new MacBook Pro, OLED is finally coming to Mac.

The redesigned MacBook Pro with OLED is expected to offer truer blacks, improved contrast, and likely help out with battery life too. Here’s hoping it’s able to match the impressive tandem OLED the iPad offers.

#2: Touchscreen

Apple has long argued that the Mac doesn’t need a touchscreen, despite competing products nearly all offering touch. But rumors indicate we’re finally getting the first Mac with touch support.

The new MacBook Pro will have a touchscreen, and macOS 27 is already packed with hints that such a feature is coming. We’re expecting further software optimizations to make touch feel like a natural experience on the Mac.

Despite touch being available, macOS will remain tailored primarily for trackpad and keyboard input. Touch will be a secondary tool on the Mac, not replacing traditional input methods but rather supplementing them for users who have grown accustomed to touchscreens on iPhones, iPads, and PCs.

#3: No more notch

When Apple last redesigned the MacBook Pro in 2021, it introduced a notch design that first came to iPhone. The notch then spread to the MacBook Air too, making it a fixture of modern Mac design.

	

But the new MacBook Pro will reportedly drop the notch in favor of a hole-punch camera cutout that likely resembles what we’ve seen on iPhone Duo.

The Dynamic Island will be brought over to macOS too, making the camera cutout integrate seamlessly on the Mac like it does on iPhone. As someone who finds the notch more of an eyesore on the Mac than I ever did on iPhone, I’m excited to see the notch disappear soon.

title: Apple and Qualcomm renew global patent licensing agreement
snippet: Qualcomm and Apple have renewed their global patent licensing agreement, extending a deal that was previously set to expire in 2027. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Qualcomm and Apple have renewed their global patent licensing agreement, extending a deal that was previously set to expire in 2027. Here are the details.

Renewed deal takes effect next year

To say that Apple and Qualcomm have had a rocky relationship would be an understatement.

Once major business partners, the companies became embroiled in a sprawling legal battle in 2017 over Qualcomm’s patent licensing practices and royalty payments.

In a nutshell, Apple sued Qualcomm in U.S. federal court in early 2017, challenging Qualcomm’s patent-licensing practices and seeking nearly $1 billion in royalty rebates that Apple said Qualcomm had improperly withheld.

The lawsuit came just three days after the FTC also sued Qualcomm, alleging anticompetitive licensing practices. The complaint specifically mentioned Qualcomm’s dealings with Apple, alleging that the company offered billions of dollars in conditional rebates in exchange for Apple exclusively using Qualcomm modem chips in new iPhones and iPads.

A few months later, Qualcomm countersued Apple, accusing the company of breaching agreements and interfering with its relationships with iPhone and iPad manufacturers.

The dispute ended in 2019, when Apple and Qualcomm agreed to drop all litigation against each other worldwide.

As part of the settlement, Apple made an undisclosed payment to Qualcomm that, among other things, resolved a dispute over royalty payments Apple had withheld during the legal battle. The companies also entered into a six-year global patent licensing agreement and a separate multiyear chipset supply deal.

That licensing agreement took effect on April 1, 2019, and included an option for Apple to extend it for another two years. Apple ultimately exercised that option, extending the agreement through March 2027.

Today, Qualcomm announced that the companies have renewed the agreement once again, with the new deal taking effect on April 1, 2027.

The full press release read:

Qualcomm Incorporated today announced the renewal of its global patent license agreement with Apple, effective April 1, 2027.

“We are pleased to extend the Apple license agreement,” said John Han, Executive Vice President and General Manager of Qualcomm Technology Licensing (QTL).

The company did not disclose how long the renewed agreement will remain in effect, while Apple has yet to comment on the renewal.

It is worth noting that today’s announcement is unrelated to Apple’s use of Qualcomm modems on iPhones, something that has been widely discussed recently, as Apple used a Qualcomm modem in the U.S. version of the iPhone 18 Pro Max while relying on its own C2 modem elsewhere.

Apple has not officially commented on what its modem plans will look like going forward, but the expectation has been that the company will eventually move away from Qualcomm modems altogether.

title: Apple Podcasts will soon let creators offer exclusive videos to subscribers
snippet: Apple announced this week that creators will soon be able to offer video through Apple Podcasts Subscriptions, “including subscriber-exclusive episodes, ad-free video, early access, and bonus content.” Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple announced this week that creators will soon be able to offer video through Apple Podcasts Subscriptions, “including subscriber-exclusive episodes, ad-free video, early access, and bonus content.” Here are the details.

Apple Podcasts Subscriptions to get support for video

Back in 2021, Apple announced Apple Podcasts Subscriptions. This service lets creators offer paid subscriptions to their shows in exchange for perks such as ad-free listening, bonus episodes, early access, and subscriber-only content.

Since then, creators have been able to offer paid subscriptions through Apple Podcasts to listeners in more than 170 countries and regions.

With the podcast market increasingly shifting toward video, Apple has been expanding the format across its platform.

Earlier this year, Apple introduced a new HLS-based video podcast experience that lets users seamlessly switch between watching and listening, view episodes full-screen, download videos for offline viewing, and more.

More recently, with iOS 27 and its other software updates, Apple expanded video support in Apple Podcasts with features including read-along transcripts, chapters, media links, and playback on Mac and Apple TV.

Now, Apple has announced that video is coming to Apple Podcasts Subscriptions as well.

This means creators will be able to offer subscriber-exclusive video episodes, ad-free video, early access, and bonus video content through the same subscription system currently used for premium audio.

From Apple’s announcement:

Since Apple Podcasts Subscriptions launched, creators have built direct-to-listener businesses around premium audio. Adding video opens new opportunities for you to connect with your audiences and grow your business.

A new way to grow your business: Apple Podcasts Subscriptions already help creators build direct-to-listener businesses around premium audio. With the introduction of video, you have new ways to connect with audiences and expand your business directly on Apple Podcasts.

Streamlined delivery: Deliver both audio and video seamlessly without maintaining separate offerings or workflows.

A familiar Apple experience: Audiences can discover and enjoy premium video across Apple devices and the web, wherever and however they choose to tune in.

Apple says it is currently working with hosting providers to make this integration seamless and will share more details “in the coming months.”

title: Google Maps update shows traffic lights and stop signs at your next turn on Android Auto, more
snippet: Google Maps is rolling out a new update on Android Auto that makes it easier to know what to expect at your next turn, with a visual indicator to show upcoming traffic lights or stop signs. more…
fullText:
Google Maps is rolling out a new update on Android Auto that makes it easier to know what to expect at your next turn, with a visual indicator to show upcoming traffic lights or stop signs.

It’s been around six years since Google Maps started showing traffic lights and stop signs along your route, but a new tweak gives these more relevance to your actual route. Where Maps previously showed these as fixed parts of the map, there’s a new pop-up that shows what to expect at upcoming intersections.

	

Alongside the floating name of the street at your next turn, Google Maps on Android Auto now also highlights whether you’ll see a traffic light or a stop sign at that intersection. We first observed this behavior earlier this week, and it’s been showing consistently in the time since. It’s also showing on the phone directly, which means iPhone users seeing the update will likely also see this on CarPlay.

It’s a subtle tweak, but it’s also a very glanceable way to give drivers a better idea of what to expect at a coming intersection, which could be invaluable if you’re driving around an unfamiliar area.

	

Like many visual updates, this is likely a server-side update for Google Maps. Let us know in the comments below if you’re seeing this update.

snippet: Apple has redesigned the Apple Pay checkout flow in iOS 27 for apps and websites. The changes make it easier to switch between different payment cards and see key details about the order you’re placing. more…
fullText:
Apple has redesigned the Apple Pay checkout flow in iOS 27 for apps and websites. The changes make it easier to switch between different payment cards and see key details about the order you’re placing.

In iOS 27, you can now swipe between payment cards right on the main Apple Pay interface. You can also tap a card to view a grid-style interface that shows all your available Apple Pay cards in one place.

Apple explains:

Apple Pay is introducing an updated design for users when they check out on the web and in apps. The design allows them to seamlessly swipe to switch cards, conveniently surfacing important information about their eligible cards in Apple Wallet — including rewards, balances, debit account balance, pay later options, and more — so they can make more informed payment decisions.

Merchants and developers have control over what appears on the Apple Pay payment sheet, depending on the exact information they need to complete your order.

The iOS 26 version of the Apple Pay checkout flow has been criticized for being unintuitive. For instance, people often tapped the wrong thing when trying to switch between payment cards. The instinct is to tap the card itself, but in iOS 26, that would take you to the address-editing interface. You’d have to tap a separate button at the bottom to actually switch to a different card. iOS 27 streamlines all of this and makes it a lot clearer.

What do you think of the new Apple Pay interface for apps and websites in iOS 27? Let us know down in the comments.

title: This is my top feature request for the upcoming A20 Pro iPad mini
snippet: For the past year, we’ve been looking forward to a new iPad mini refresh, and it’s sounding like its just around the corner. A new leak last week from Aaron Perris unveiled that the product should feature an A20 Pro chip and thinner bezels, and we already know it’ll feature OLED and a water resistant design. While those upgrades are excellent, I have one major thing I want from the next iPad mini, and it has to do with software. more…
fullText:
For the past year, we’ve been looking forward to a new iPad mini refresh, and it’s sounding like its just around the corner. A new leak last week from Aaron Perris unveiled that the product should feature an A20 Pro chip and thinner bezels, and we already know it’ll feature OLED and a water resistant design.

While those upgrades are excellent, I have one major thing I want from the next iPad mini, and it has to do with software.

After seeing the iPhone Duo, I’m amazed at how well Apple mastered the multitasking on the device. Multitasking on iPad has always felt like a mess to me, and iPhone Duo just feels elegant.

On such a small screen, having proper windowing on the iPad mini never felt appropriate. Users likely aren’t overlapping many windows on iPad mini. That’s why I want Apple to steal one nifty feature from the iPhone Duo: split screen with picture in picture.

	

I mean really, this is such an excellent experience. Currently, there’s no way on iPad mini to make a picture in picture window take up the entire width of the device in portrait, and even if there were, you’d either have to have it block some of your app, or manually align the sizing using windowing.

Bringing video and app split view to the iPad mini‘s display seems like a no brainer to me, especially given the fact that the iPhone Duo and iPad mini share similar aspect ratios. At least personally, I’d use an iPad mini in portrait a lot more if this feature existed.

title: Apple Watch Ultra 4 includes a new watch face bezel option
snippet: Apple Watch Ultra includes a few more ways to customize your watch face than Series models. These include Ultra-only faces, colors and fonts, and a bezel-type complication. Apple Watch Ultra 4 goes even further, adding a new option in the bezel configuration category. more…
fullText:
Apple Watch Ultra includes a few more ways to customize your watch face than Series models. These include Ultra-only faces, colors and fonts, and a bezel-type complication. Apple Watch Ultra 4 goes even further, adding a new option in the bezel configuration category.

Readiness is a new bezel option on Apple Watch Ultra 4

Both Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 introduce the new Readiness app. This uses data like fitness activity, vitals, and sleep score to present you with a Readiness score.

Overnight vitals include heart rate, respiratory rate, wrist temperature, and recovery HRV. Daytime vitals include heart rate and recovery HRV. 

Apple Watch Ultra 4 faces that support displaying bezel information add Readiness as a new watch face configuration. Bezel options now include:

None

Seconds

Depth

Elevation

Training

Readiness

The Readiness bezel option puts your numerical score and description at the bottom of the watch face.

Four bars wrap the edge of the watch face, showing the different readiness score categories, while a dot indicates where your score fits within that category.

Watch faces like Modular Ultra and the new Siri Modular face support displaying the bezel configuration.

	

If you’re looking for a way to focus on your readiness score, the new bezel configuration is a great way to keep track of the number.

Since readiness can change throughout the day, it may be worth having front-and-center for a lot of users.

Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 are both available now.
