title: Ninja CrushBoss Review: The Perfect Blender If You Hate Chopping Vegetables
snippet: The food processor and blender attachments are handy, while other elements feel like overkill.
fullText:
Where to put it? That’s the question that stops many of us from buying another countertop appliance. In my small kitchen, every new piece of equipment means pushing another one out. Larger kitchens have more room to work with, but even they can end up more cluttered than one would like.

This modestly sized blender does far more than blend.  John Carlsen/CNET

Eventually, you need to decide if you’ll use an appliance often enough to justify getting it. In my case, I’m much more likely to choose a multipurpose product like an Instant Pot pressure cooker or an air fryer. Perhaps this is why I was excited to test out the Ninja CrushBoss, which combines a large blender, food processor and small smoothie blender into a single device. I spent the two weeks using a sample unit from Ninja in my kitchen, and I’m eager to share my thoughts. 

4 appliances in 1? Well, kind of

The main appeal of the Ninja CrushBoss is that it comes with three vessels: a 72-ounce blender pitcher, a 64-ounce food processor bowl and a 26-ounce smoothie tumbler.

CrushBoss isn’t Ninja’s first attempt at an all-in-one kitchen system, as the Ninja Detect, Ninja Professional Plus and Ninja Foodi Power Blender all attempt similar feats. What sets Ninja CrushBoss apart are the PrecisionDice and MultiBlade Disc attachments for the food processor bowl, plus a better smoothie tumbler design than previous models.

			

More from CNET

Similarly, the blender’s preset programs change depending on which vessel you attach to the 1,850-watt base motor, with each program running automatically to achieve the desired results. You can rotate the outer ring of the small LCD screen to choose your setting, then make the final selection by pressing the top of the screen inward. It’s not a touchscreen, but it’s easy enough to use once you learn the controls.

Intelligent blending features, PrepIQ and SmoothSense, track the type and consistency of what you’re blending, but I didn’t notice a difference compared to the preset programs or custom speed controls.John Carlsen/CNET

There isn’t much that’s special about the large blender pitcher, which uses largely the same design as other standalone Ninja blenders. It comes with a single blade assembly and presets for mincing, small chopping and large chopping. The smoothie tumbler is similarly simple, with its small blade assembly supporting ice crushing, blending and smoothie presets. Compared to older tumblers, the Travel Tumbler’s main upgrades are a better carrying handle, flip-top lid, and large smoothie straw — it’s more like a Stanley cup than a NutriBullet personal blender.

Last but not least is the food processor, which has the most accessories, including a chopping blade, dough blade, MultiBlade Disc, and the PrecisionDice assembly. Where the Ninja Detect’s food processor included reversible stainless steel discs, the MultiBlade attachment is largely plastic, with specific inserts depending on the model you choose. The model I tested came with inserts for thick slices, crinkle-cut slices and shredding — Ninja also sells inserts for thin slices, french fries and julienning.

While I understand that the plastic MultiBlade Disc and inserts reduce the amount of stainless steel in the package, I can’t help but wonder about their long-term durability compared to all-metal discs.John Carlsen/CNET

I call it a kind of four-in-one appliance because the smoothie tumbler’s main benefits are, naturally, smoother blending consistency than the large pitcher and greater travel portability with the included lid and smoothie straw. You can still use the large pitcher for family-size smoothies and anything too big for the other two vessels, so adding a blending function to each vessel is largely superfluous. Similarly, the dicing kit is hardly an appliance on its own, since you’ll see it on other food processor brands like KitchenAid and Breville.

How useful is the Ninja CrushBoss?

The point of the cheese test was to find the food processor’s limits, so I’m happy to report the motor safety cutoff and error messages worked as intended when I stressed the unit too much.John Carlsen/CNET

Of the three vessels, I spent the most time with the food processor. I used the PrecisionDice attachment to prepare a fruit salad, which went very smoothly and had no issues with mango, watermelon, strawberries and pineapple. I pureed some blackberries with the food processor’s chopping blade to add more texture to the salad, though the smoothie attachment was ultimately a better option for crushing the blackberry seeds.

Next, I swapped the dicing attachment for the MultiBlade and sliced potatoes and cucumbers with the normal and crinkle-cut attachments. Again, the results were very good. Things were a little less consistent when I processed carrots and cabbage with the shredder for a quick coleslaw, as some bits of each remained unprocessed between the blade and lid. The amount of unprocessed vegetables was minimal, so I tossed them into a bowl of ramen instead of chopping them by hand for the coleslaw.

To give the food processor a proper workout, I brought out the cheddar cheese and ran it through the shredder, slicer, and dicer. As you might suspect, the cheese worked best with the shredder, with very little waste and no clogs. The other two attachments are less suitable for cheese, with the slicing disc producing passable slices. However, I clogged the dicing tool when I tried to make cheese cubes. I ultimately succeeded with some tiny cubes, but I don’t recommend it. 

	

			

	

			

									

						Best Blenders We Tested in 2026					

							

		

While I didn’t use the dough blade attachment much, it seemed good for mixing bread dough into a state where I could knead it by hand. I ran three cycles using the dough preset — though I admit the last cycle was because I forgot to add an ingredient. One reason I finished by hand was that I could hear the motor straining a bit toward the end of the second and third cycles.

Even if I’m not 100% on board with using it for dense bread dough, the unit is plenty powerful for cookie dough and cake batter.John Carlsen/CNET

I suspect the CrushBoss can handle the job, as the manual says it can hold up to 2 pounds of dough and shut off if necessary, but it took only a minute of hand-kneading after processing to reach the consistency I wanted. My advice: Listen to your machine and avoid tasks that trigger the auto-shutoff too often. Fortunately, my testing didn’t surface any problems with the system’s durability.

Beyond the food processor bowl, little stood out about the blender pitcher and smoothie tumbler attachments. Each did well with various levels of blending, pureeing and ice crushing, but nothing so outstanding that my ancient Oster blender couldn’t also do. The biggest advantages over my modest blender are the pitcher’s size — even if it’s more than I need in my kitchen — and the tumbler’s portability. Ninja says CrushBoss isn’t suitable for hot blending, so you can’t safely use it with hot liquids.

The challenge of modular kitchen systems like Ninja CrushBoss

Somewhat paradoxically, the modular nature of the Ninja CrushBoss is also its biggest weakness — at least for me.John Carlsen/CNET

Although I’m happy that I don’t have to store three motorized bases for separate specialty appliances, all of Ninja’s vessels and attachments are bulky enough that they’d take up an entire shelf in my kitchen cabinets. There’s not really a safe way to store the extremely sharp food processor discs, so I ultimately kept them in a carrying case for a massage gun I threw out ages ago. Fortunately, you can safely store the largest blender blade assemblies in each vessel.

The other challenge is that while all of the attachments are dishwasher-safe, that only applies to the top rack. My older dishwasher’s top rack isn’t adjustable, so I can’t fit any of the vessels inside and I have to wash them all by hand. This isn’t a problem I experience with the glass jar of my Oster blender, or the slightly smaller vessel of the Tribest Backspin I tested in 2025. At least the other parts fit, which made cleanup much more manageable.

My point in calling these out isn’t to discourage anyone interested in the CrushBoss, but to note that storage space and dishwasher space still matter before you buy.

Should you buy the Ninja CrushBoss?

The CrushBoss’s value becomes more apparent as your food volume increases.John Carlsen/CNET

As I used the Ninja CrushBoss 4-in-1, I kept coming back to one central question: “Who is this for?” Ultimately, it’s a harder question to answer than I thought. I have no problem recommending each function separately — blending, smoothies, dicing and food processing — because it seems to do all of these well enough.

For example, this particular setup should work well for two types of households: large families and meal preppers. I grew up in a large family, and having an appliance to prepare a huge amount of ingredients for every meal is a no-brainer. Another group that might benefit is the meal-prepper, regardless of household size.

Still, selling everything together in a single kit is excessive for someone like me, who has a small apartment. I have plenty of travel cups for smoothies and rarely need to process large amounts of food. Ninja thankfully offers various CrushBoss configurations and will most likely sell the attachments separately down the line, like with its older products. Personally, I’d love a configuration with only a large pitcher and food processor — I don’t need a smoothie tumbler.

At $320, the Ninja CrushBoss 4-in-1 costs about what you’d pay for separate Ninja appliances, but it is pricier than previous generations of Ninja’s modular kitchen systems, even without the dicing kit. This is a drop in the bucket compared to getting similar attachments for a Vitamix Ascent X. Despite my personal reservations, I think the Ninja CrushBoss 4-in-1 is a great idea, especially for folks looking to consolidate multiple specialty appliances into a single modular system. It taps into the reason why people love the classic KitchenAid stand mixer, and that’s a good thing.

title: Apple Notes keeps getting better, here’s what’s new in iOS 27
snippet: iOS 27 adds new features for CarPlay, the Messages app, and a lot more, including a handful of Apple Notes upgrades. Here’s what’s new for Apple Notes in iOS 27. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 adds new features for CarPlay, the Messages app, and a lot more, including a handful of Apple Notes upgrades. Here’s what’s new for Apple Notes in iOS 27. 

Divider line added for organizing your notes

Joining the many different formatting tools already available in Apple Notes, iOS 27 lets you add divider lines to your notes.

It’s pretty simple. Just tap where you want the line to go, open the edit menu, and choose the new ‘Insert Divider Line’ option.

Divider lines are a great new way to organize content in a note, and a welcome addition to the Notes toolset.

Section links

Section links are now supported in iOS 27’s Notes app, letting you build a table of contents or other structure to navigate longer notes with ease.

To create a section link, select text inside your and open the edit menu. From there, hit ‘Add Link’ to see a new option: Link to Section.

This opens a menu where you’ll find all of the headings and subheadings currently found in your note. You can tap to select one, which will create a direct link to that section embedded in your text.

Create and add to notes with Siri AI

The single Notes upgrade I’m most excited about in iOS 27 involves Siri.

Apple’s new Siri AI lets you quickly, seamlessly add information to a new note or existing note in Apple Notes.

You can do this, for example, with any answer Siri provides in the new Siri app. Or you can do what I did (seen above) where I asked Siri to take a poorly formatted list and reformat it, then add it to a new note.

This works for existing notes too, just tell Siri which note you want to add to. Siri has offered some limited Notes capabilities in the past, but the new integration is a big upgrade.

Copy and paste Markdown

Last year in iOS 26, Apple Notes gained support for importing and exporting Markdown.

If you’re unfamiliar with Markdown, it’s a text formatting syntax created by John Gruber. With Markdown, you can write in plain text using special syntax for headings, links, lists, bold and italics formatting, and more. It’s a popular tool for writers who publish content online.

With iOS 27, Apple Notes is getting even more Markdown-friendly.

Now when you paste Markdown-formatted text into a note, it’s automatically converted into rich text. There are zero extra steps required. And if you want to copy text from your note as Markdown, there’s a new Copy as Markdown option you’ll find in the edit menu.

Image Playground upgrades

iOS 27 brings big upgrades to the Image Playground app and its underlying AI models. And since Image Playground is a key built-in feature of the Notes app, Notes users benefit too.

Per Apple’s press release:

Image Playground offers new powerful ways for users to bring their imagination to life. They can create high-quality images in virtually any style, now including photorealistic, thanks to a new generative model that runs on Private Cloud Compute. This is a major transformation for image generation across platforms. And generated images will automatically include a hidden SynthID watermark to identify them as AI-generated.

Apple Notes in iOS 27: wrap-up

Notes also features a variety of smaller UI refinements in iOS 27, including:

Newly refreshed app icon

Liquid Glass updates for buttons, menus, and more

Shared folder at top of folders list adds new icon

Individual shared folders and notes have updated icons too

title: The iPhone 18 Pro: The best and final iteration of the current form factor?
snippet: There’s a running joke that Apple always breathlessly announces that each year’s iPhone Pro is “the best iPhone we’ve ever made,” as if that were in some way surprising. But I do think that there’s some poignancy to the iPhone 18 Pro, because if the rumors about next year’s model are true, this could be the final iteration of the form factor that began with the iPhone X back in 2017. Specifically, we’re expecting next year to see the next big step toward that “single slab of glass” vision which will end the era of evolutionary change we’ve seen over the last decade … more…
fullText:
There’s a running joke that Apple always breathlessly announces that each year’s iPhone Pro is “the best iPhone we’ve ever made,” as if that were in some way surprising. But I do think that there’s some poignancy to the iPhone 18 Pro, because if the rumors about next year’s model are true, this could be the final iteration of the form factor that began with the iPhone X back in 2017.

Specifically, we’re expecting next year to see the next big step toward that “single slab of glass” vision which will end the era of evolutionary change we’ve seen over the last decade …

The evolution of the iPhone Pro models

If you were to line up every model from the iPhone 12 Pro to the iPhone 16 Pro, I think many people would struggle to tell the difference visually bar the switch from notch to Dynamic Island in 2022. The iPhone 17 Pro is still only an exception due to the extended camera island and Cosmic Orange option.

Of course, each model had new features, but I think even here it’s fair to say that unless a specific one has particular relevance to you personally, you really need to jump at least two or three generations before an upgrade amounts to a significantly better experience.

This in no way a criticism of Apple. The reality is that premium smartphones are a mature technology, at least in the conventional form-factor. We don’t see massive differences between successive generations because there’s only so much that can be done to improve them on an annual basis.

Apple is now experimenting with different form factors, starting with the iPhone Air and now, of course, the iPhone Duo – and we’re expecting another major design leap next year, in the form of a 20th anniversary model.

How exactly Apple will position next year’s design remains somewhat unclear. It was initially suggested that it would be a standalone model, distinct from the iPhone 19 Pro, while other reports suggest that it will be next year’s Pro model. There’s also the question of whether Apple will use sequential numbering or skip a number to mark the occasion, so it might instead be called the iPhone 20 Pro.

Personally, I do suspect that it will be the new iPhone Pro design, whether Apple calls it the 19 or 20. If this is correct, then the iPhone 18 Pro will be the final iteration of the form factor we’ve had for half a dozen years. 

I’m jumping two generations from the iPhone 16 Pro, so I’m going to separately list the new-to-me features introduced by each year’s models. I’m skipping improvements I see as trivial or completely irrelevant to my use, like 7-core GPU over 6-core and GenLock.

iPhone 17 Pro features carried forward

Center Stage front camera, for photos and video calls

Ultra-stabilised video

Dual capture

Telephoto lens up from 5x to 8x 

Telephoto sensor up from 12 MP to 48 MP

ProRes RAW video

Better battery life

Faster charging

New to iPhone 18 Pro

Wider maximum aperture on the main camera lens

Variable aperture main camera lens

Pro camera controls (aperture, shutter speed, white balance, histogram)

Photographic Styles v3

Smart focus tracking

Cinematic mode effects from standard video

Tap to zoom and rotate on the front camera

Smaller Dynamic Island, enabling three live activities

(Even) better battery life

(Even) faster charging

My personal … focus

Personally, there are five features I will be focusing on in my early usage.

Variable-aperture lens

While the headline feature is that variable aperture lens, I’ve said before that we probably shouldn’t expect too much from it. The maximum aperture is only marginally wider on such a small sensor, so I’m not expecting to see much difference in terms of shallow depth of field.

However, the maximum aperture does let in a little more light, amounting to around two-thirds of a stop. How much difference that will make remains to be seen, but it should translate to shorter Night Mode exposures. Since this is a feature I use a lot, often handheld, then I am looking forward to trying this.

Pro camera controls

The ability to control shutter speed will definitely have its uses for things like panning shots. And it will certainly be useful to be able to take full control of white balance. I’m also expecting the histogram to be useful when manually setting the exposure.

Photographic Styles v3

I’m generally not a filters kind of guy when it comes to either taking photos or editing them on the iPhone, preferring to do any editing using conventional adjustments afterwards. For that reason, I rarely used the existing Photographic Styles feature and don’t expect to make much use of the latest iteration either. But I must say I am intrigued by the film setting, so I’ll certainly be experimenting with this.

Smart focus tracking

One of the biggest weaknesses with autofocus when it comes to video occurs when the subject briefly passes behind something else and the camera can switch focus to the obstruction. Smart Focus Tracking claims to solve this problem, so I will certainly be putting this to the test.

Cinematic Mode effects from standard video

	

It’s less than a couple of months since I said that Apple appeared to have forgotten about Cinematic video mode. I said that was a great pity because, if Cinematic Mode video worked well, it would be an absolute game-changer for the practicality of the iPhone as a camera for more serious video work. So far, it has been frustratingly close but no cigar.

However, it appears I was wrong: one of the new iPhone 18 features is that the cinematic video effects can be applied to videos shot in standard mode.

It’s certainly very handy that we no longer need to decide in advance whether or not to use the mode, but what most interests me is that Apple is again paying attention to the feature. This suggests that it is indeed being shown some love, and we therefore can expect it to continue to improve in much the way Portrait mode did for still photos. I’m very much looking forward to testing this.

These, then, are the features I think could potentially make the most difference to me. How about you? If you’ve upgraded to the iPhone 18 Pro, what features drove your decision? Please share in the comments.

title: Square now integrates with Apple Business to improve Maps listings
snippet: Square has announced a new integration with Apple Business that should make Apple Maps better for both businesses and users. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Square has announced a new integration with Apple Business that should make Apple Maps better for both businesses and users. Here are the details.

Square integration lets businesses easily keep Apple Maps listings up to date with accurate info

Have you ever been frustrated to learn that an Apple Maps business listing has outdated info? Maybe the listed hours are inaccurate, or it has an error in the address, phone number, and so on.

Square’s new integration with Apple Business should help. From the announcement:

Square today announced a new integration with Apple that enables Square sellers to connect their locations to Apple Business from their Square Dashboard, so they can seamlessly manage and synchronize key business location information that appears on Apple Maps. Rather than managing multiple channels separately, sellers can now maintain their Apple presence alongside the rest of their business in Square. The integration makes it easier for sellers to ensure Apple users see up-to-date and accurate information across Apple Maps, Siri AI, Apple Wallet and other Apple apps.

Per Square, this integration provides several key benefits to business owners. It lets them:

Manage their brand and add a logo across connected locations, allowing them to enhance and extend their brand presence to Apple Maps place cards, directly from Square Dashboard.

Automatically sync key business details for each connected location, such as hours, address, and phone number, so this information stays up-to-date and accurate across Apple Maps, Siri AI, Apple Wallet, and other Apple apps and services without manual updates.

Turn discovery into engagement across connected locations with action links such as Menu, Order, Pickup, Delivery, Book, or Schedule Appointment, so customers can take action directly from an Apple Maps place card.

The partnership sounds like a clear win for businesses, since so many already rely on Square. But it should result in a better Apple Maps experience for users over time too.

Business owners can learn more about the Square and Apple Business integration at squareup.com/partnerships/applebusiness.

Elevate your iPhone 18 Pro and Apple Watch setup with AirPods Pro 3 at $50 off

One of the best early fall Prime Day deals live right now has Apple’s latest flagship AirPods Pro 3 down at $50 off the list price. And with the new iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch Series 12, and Ultra 4 out in the wild, AirPods Pro 3 might be the best way to elevate the experience. 

Amazon is currently offering Apple’s AirPods Pro 3 down at $199 shipped. 

Regularly $249, this is $50 off, slightly below the deal price at Best Buy, and the best deal we can find right now that anyone can take advantage of. 

Apple did just unleash the new AirPods 5 starting from $129 with ANC included this time around, but if you want the flagship experience with the 3x ANC, a wireless charging case, longer battery life, and built-in heart rate sensor, the AirPods Pro 3 are where it’s at. You can score AirPods 5 with a Wireless Charging Case for $149, but you’re not going to get the proper sealed ANC treatment and the bonus features found on the Pro set. 

There is, of course, something to keep in mind here – this is an ongoing price drop that is carrying over into the early fall Prime Day event. And that might very well mean Amazon could drop the price lower come October 6 (or sooner) when the official Prime Big Deal Days sale begins. We have seen Amazon drop the price to $189 and $179 on a few rare occasions, and even as low as $169 during the summer Prime Day sale. This might very well be the case again in two weeks from now for the fall event, but we can’t say for sure, and the $169 offer constantly went in and out of stock.

title: These are my favorite iPhone 18 Pro & Pro Max cases so far [Video]
snippet: The new iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max have been out for a week, and they have been amazing devices to use and test. While the actual footprint and visual design remain unchanged, Apple spiced things up with new colors like Glacier, Burgundy, and a true Deep Black version. These colors are a nice new addition to the iPhone lineup, but, of course, the main question I get asked is: What case should I get to protect my new $ 1,200+ device? Luckily, there are already hundreds of case options for the new 18 Pro lineup, and I have been lucky enough to test a bunch. I know cases are purely subjective and a matter of preference, but I figured I would share some of my favorites! more…
fullText:
The new iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max have been out for a week, and they have been amazing devices to use and test. While the actual footprint and visual design remain unchanged, Apple spiced things up with new colors like Glacier, Burgundy, and a true Deep Black version. These colors are a nice new addition to the iPhone lineup, but, of course, the main question I get asked is: What case should I get to protect my new $ 1,200+ device? Luckily, there are already hundreds of case options for the new 18 Pro lineup, and I have been lucky enough to test a bunch. I know cases are purely subjective and a matter of preference, but I figured I would share some of my favorites!

Be sure to check out our hands-on video with all of these cases to see which one would be best for you!

Pitaka Edge case

I have always leaned towards ultra-thin and minimal cases. I like being able to protect my iPhone while still feeling its actual design. If thinness and lightweight cases are what you are into then Pitaka’s Edge cases are the first option I would consider. You get:

Ultra-thin and lightweight aramid fiber construction

Improved camera protection with a raised camera lip and PitaTap camera control cover

Built-in MagSafe magnets for added strength

Precise cutouts for the buttons, speakers, and USB-C port

Available in a ton of different designs

Even at just 20g and 1mm in thickness, this case offers a ton of protection and rigidity. Pitaka’s Edge case is available today on Amazon for $59 and comes in 10+ colors and designs. 

Nomad Sport Case

Nomad’s Sport Case gives you that perfect balance of everyday protection while staying relatively thin and lightweight. I went with the Lunar Gret color to contrast with the Deep Black iPhone, and it looks fantastic. This case brings:

Smooth, soft-touch exterior with a protective construction

Tactile metal buttons with a textured finish

Microfiber interior lining to help protect your iPhone

Raised camera and screen edges for additional protection

Built-in MagSafe compatibility and a dedicated Camera Control cover

If you want a high-quality, no-frills case that keeps your phone protected while still making it look awesome, I would look into the Nomad Sport case. It’s available on Amazon for $55!

Xtremm Inno E-Ink Case

This is easily one of the most unique and fun cases that I have ever reviewed. The Xtremm Inno  puts a color E-Ink display on the rear of the iPhone that is 100% customizable. You can put any image you want on there, like family photos, team logos, anime characters, literally anything. It’s all done via NFC, so the case does not need a battery, power, or Bluetooth, keeping it as thin and light as any other regular case. It feels like magic. 

Customizable color E-Ink display on the back of the case

NFC technology for transferring images from your iPhone

Support for personal photos and AI-generated designs

Raised camera protection and dedicated Camera Control cover

Built-in MagSafe compatibility despite the rear display

We have a whole video on this to show it off. I recommend watching it before purchasing, just to see how cool this looks! It’s available on Amazon for $75 and comes in five different colors for the new iPhone 18 Pro lineup. 

Rokform Crystal Case

Now, if you need something a bit more rugged with added protection but still want to show off that new burgundy iPhone color, then Rokform is a great choice. Not only is it extremely protective, but It Also has Rokform’s proprietary locking system in addition to MagSafe. This makes it even more useful for someone who needs to securely mount their iPhone on a bike, motorcycle, or other devices that require more than just magnets. 

Rugged construction with reinforced corners and raised edges

Transparent back panel that shows off your iPhone’s color

Rokform’s proprietary twist-lock mounting system

Built-in MagSafe compatibility

Full camera plateau protection with a dedicated Camera Control cover

The Rokform Crystal Case is available on Amazon for $69. They also have their own ecosystem of mounts and attachments worth checking out. 

BodyGuardz Weave Case

This is a brand that I had not heard much about until this year. They have been around for a while, but they just released their new Weave line, and I love the design, texture, and multifunctionality of it all. You get:

Textured woven exterior with a comfortable grip

Integrated kickstand 

Speaker channels designed to direct audio forward

Raised edges for screen and camera protection

Built-in MagSafe 

The speaker directional feature is something I had not seen before, and it actually makes a nice difference. Because of how the speaker cutout is designed, it directs the audio right at you rather than to your left or right. Very unique touch! The BodyGuardz Weave is available on Amazon for $59

Andar Aspen

If you are someone who misses the old iPhone leather cases of years past, then Andar is the next best alternative. I have been using their cases for years, and they are some of the best leather cases on the market. You get:

Genuine leather exterior that develops a unique patina over time and smells fantastic 

Soft microfiber interior lining 

Raised edges around the display and camera for additional protection

Dedicated Camera Control cover and tactile metal buttons

Built-in MagSafe compatibility and multiple color options

Their new black color matches the Deep Black iPhone so well that it almost makes the iPhone disappear in the shadows. They have over 10 colors to choose from, and these cases just get better with time. The Andar Aspen Case is available for $70 and can be purchased directly through Andar.

Spigen Nano Pop Case

Spigen’s Nano Pop case is a great option if you are looking for something that will color-match and enhance your new iPhone. It has a two-tone design that looks especially nice with the new Burgundy iPhone, and it also has uniquely textured sides for additional grip in the hand. The Pop case gives you:

Two-tone design with contrasting colors

Flexible, rubberized construction with textured sides for additional grip

Raised edges and protection around the entire camera plateau

Dedicated Camera Control cover

Built-in lanyard attachment point

This one is the most budget-friendly of the bunch as well, sitting at just $21 directly from Amazon

Final take

As I mentioned in the intro, cases are highly subjective purchases. It is almost like clothing but for your phone. There is no right or wrong answer to any of these, just a matter of what you think works and looks best. All of these have their own unique selling points and differentiators, and they come from very reputable brands, so there is no going wrong with any of them. I personally like to keep it as thin and light as possible, while I know my brother likes his cases bulky and protective. 

Be sure to catch our video on these, as we go hands-on with all of these cases, and leave a comment on some other brands I need to check out. I would love to give you guys a round two of my favorite cases later in the year. For those people waiting for the iPhone Duo, we will also have something similar for the new device.

title: Watch a YouTuber Emulate PlayStation 5 Games on an Xbox Series X
snippet: He told CNET he wanted to see if those games could play on the hardware, so he worked it out.
fullText:
The ultimate console crossover just went from a gamer’s pipe dream to reality. Modder Devran “Cosmo” Uenal recently posted a video on YouTube in which he plays a PlayStation 5 emulator on an Xbox Series X. He told CNET in a message that he wanted to see if he could get those games to play on the Xbox hardware.

“There was only one way to find out, so I did it,” he wrote. 

Uenal said in the video that he ran an experimental Xbox port of the open-source PlayStation 5 emulator KytyPS5. That emulator — which is itself a heavily modified version of another emulator — is meant to be run on PC, so getting it to run on Xbox took some effort.

		

			

Uenal wrote that to make this project easier, he looked for less demanding games to run in the emulator. In the video, he has the option to play PlayStation 5 versions of Gex Trilogy, Hellboy Web of Wyrd, Marvel Cosmic Invasion and Quake 2 on an Xbox Series X. He ultimately boots up Quake 2 in the video.

“Quake 2 piqued my interest,” he wrote to CNET. “It’s a game I played almost 30 years ago on much older hardware, so I knew it would be a good candidate for testing.”

Quake 2 runs at 20 to 40 frames per second for most of Uenal’s video, with a few significant stutters. After watching this video, I booted up Quake 2 on Xbox Game Pass’s cloud streaming and didn’t experience lag or other issues. However, it’s still impressive that Uenal could get the PlayStation 5 version of that game to work on Xbox hardware.

“I hear ‘that’s impossible’ a lot, but for me that’s just fuel for motivation,” Uenal told CNET.

Representatives for Xbox and PlayStation didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

In another video, Uenal shows the PlayStation 5 user interface screen running on an Xbox, and you can see the option to play the PlayStation version of Grand Theft Auto 5.

According to tech and gaming website BGR, GTA 5 is “surprisingly playable” on the PC version of KytyPS5, so we could see a video in the future of Uenal playing a PlayStation version of GTA 5 on an Xbox. We might even get that before Rockstar releases Grand Theft Auto 6. 

Emulators are software that can mimic other hardware. In this case, the software allows you to play PlayStation 5 games on Xbox. According to Indiana law firm McNeely Law, emulators themselves aren’t illegal. However, their potential for playing pirated games raises legal concerns.

“It may be legal in certain, limited circumstances for a gamer to re-create a game they have purchased into a file playable by their emulator, it is generally illegal to share or download any video game files for use via emulator,” the law firm wrote online.

Because emulators fall into a legal gray area, I don’t recommend using them. Don’t get yourself in trouble just to play a nearly 30-year-old game like Quake 2. 

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Zachary McAuliffe
						

						

							Senior writer						
					

											

								

											Zach began writing for CNET in November, 2021 after writing for a broadcast news station in his hometown, Cincinnati, for five years. You can usually find him hanging out with his wife, son and dog. You can reach him at zmcauliffe@cnet.com.

title: Apple’s dimensional drawings offer a fascinating look at its product designs
snippet: Not everyone knows this (and I won’t even pretend that I did), but Apple publishes remarkably detailed dimensional drawings for dozens of its devices to help accessory makers design products around them. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Not everyone knows this (and I won’t even pretend that I did), but Apple publishes remarkably detailed dimensional drawings for dozens of its devices to help accessory makers design products around them. Here are the details.

Apple hardware, mapped in great detail

For almost 30 years, Jason Kottke has been one of my main sources for interesting content on (and off) the internet that I would most certainly have never discovered otherwise.

A few days ago, he published this post, linking to Apple’s Dimensional Drawings section inside the Accessories area of its developer website.

In a nutshell, this is a repository of incredibly detailed technical drawings of what currently amounts to 96 devices, including the new iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12, and the AirPods 5.

The list also includes products like the MacBook Neo and the Siri Remote, as well as accessories such as AirTag, AirPods charging cases, and even the Apple Vision Pro’s ZEISS Optical Inserts.

Each document includes precise measurements for everything from the device’s overall dimensions and curves to its buttons, cameras, sensors, speakers, and connectors, along with detailed keepout zones and instructions showing where certain materials should not be placed.

While these documents are meant for accessory makers, they’re also likely to appeal to anyone with even a mild interest in hardware, industrial design, or simply the kind of attention to detail that generally draws people to Apple products in the first place.

For Apple’s Dimensional Drawings, follow this link. And if you don’t already, make sure to start following kottke.org.

fullText:
watchOS 27.2 is coming next month with new Apple Watch features, and leaker pdfu just found a big change in the works for screenshots too.

New screenshot experience in watchOS 27.2 code takes inspiration from iPhone

Leaker pdfu has recently started sharing a variety of tidbits found in Apple code. For example, he was the first to discover the Readiness app in watchOS 27, and just yesterday leaked the UI for Siri AI on HomePod.

Today in a new post, pdfu reveals that the watchOS 27.2 beta includes code for a revamped screenshot experience on Apple Watch.

A new screenshot experience is coming to Apple Watch, inspired by iPhone.

Hidden behind a feature flag in watchOS 27.2, it lets you preview, share, or delete a screenshot right after taking it. pic.twitter.com/MT5wmDjRnq

— pdfu (@itspdfu) September 24, 2026

Currently, taking an Apple Watch screenshot simply causes the screen to flash, then the screenshot is added to your Photos library. 

The new screenshot flow imitates what’s available now on iPhone and iPad, letting you optionally share and/or delete the screenshot right away.

It’s unclear if Apple plans to implement this change in a forthcoming watchOS 27.2 beta, or if it needs more time for development. But if it doesn’t make the cut in watchOS 27.2, we’re still likely to see it come to the Apple Watch in the near future.

title: Google Photos rolling out Redact tool, Mood filters, & more
snippet: Google Photos is rolling out a handful of new features, including a Redact Markup tool and “Moods” on Android. more…
fullText:
Google Photos is rolling out a handful of new features, including a Redact Markup tool and “Moods” on Android.

The upgraded Markup tool adds three features, starting with a Redact pen that lets you blur/pixelate sensitive info in screenshots and images. There are also precise thickness sliders for the Pen and new fonts in the Text tool. This is rolling out globally to Google Photos for Android.

Moods let you easily apply a “nostalgic, vintage-inspired look” to pictures, including Crisp 35mm (film), 2000’s night (digicam), Retro contrast, Night light, Blue Haze, Any Minimalist, and Rich textures. You get slider controls, with each mood “intelligently adapt[ing] to your images.” This is rolling out globally on Android.

There are also 15 new Remix templates, including red carpet moments, whimsical birthday cards, and photo booth shots. This is rolling out in select countries on Android and iOS.

	

Google Photos is also highlighting how the Wardrobe feature is now available in Brazil, India, and the US on Android and iOS. An AI Pro or AI Ultra subscription is required. There’s also the Photos integration in Gemini Spark announced earlier this month.

title: iOS 27 lets you create your own custom iPhone wallpapers
snippet: Apple introduces new iPhone wallpapers every year, and you can download iOS 27’s additions here. But iOS 27 also adds the ability to create your own custom wallpapers. Here’s how. more…
fullText:
Apple introduces new iPhone wallpapers every year, and you can download iOS 27’s additions here. But iOS 27 also adds the ability to create your own custom wallpapers. Here’s how.

Here’s how you can create custom wallpapers in iOS 27

This year as part of iOS 27’s overall theme of major AI improvements, Apple has given its Image Playground app an overhaul.

Image Playground now offers more powerful image generation capabilities and far fewer restrictions than before. It even lets you create images that are the perfect wallpaper size.

But you don’t even need to open the Image Playground app to create wallpapers.

iOS 27 lets you create your own iPhone wallpapers right from the wallpaper picker.

Go to Settings ⇾ Wallpaper ⇾ Add New Wallpaper or long-press your Lock Screen and hit the ‘+’ button to open iOS 27’s wallpaper gallery.

New in the gallery this year, you’ll see Image Playground as an option in the top row. iOS 27 also automatically adds some AI-generated images to the Featured wallpaper section.

For example, you’ll see suggested wallpapers that are based on your own photos, but in a new style. 

In my testing of iOS 27, with no effort on my part, my iPhone prepared beautifully stylized versions of some of my favorite photos that look great as wallpapers.

Wherever you see an AI-generated wallpaper in the gallery, Apple’s new Image Playground icon appears next to it. That way, it’s always clear where the image came from.

If you like one of Apple’s suggested AI wallpapers, you can choose it and be all set.

But iOS 27 also lets you create fully custom wallpapers by hitting the Image Playground button in the top row. Image Playground will ask you to describe your image, and let you optionally choose a style or base it on an existing photo or person.

When the image is created, it’s automatically the perfect size for an iPhone wallpaper.

Have you tried iOS 27’s new wallpaper creation tool? Let us know in the comments.

title: Googlebooks will get full GeForce Now support ‘later this year’
snippet: Nvidia says Google’s new Gemini-infused laptops are slated to get GeForce Now support before the year is up, which is perfect because Googlebooks don’t exactly pack a ton of power. more…
fullText:
Nvidia says Google’s new Gemini-infused laptops are slated to get GeForce Now support before the year is up, which is perfect because Googlebooks don’t exactly pack a ton of power.

The entire Googlebook line was officially announced on September 21, spanning across Acer, Dell, ASUS, HP, and Lenovo. Each has its own draw, but they share the same baseline 16GB of RAM, up to 32GB. Each is equipped with a touchscreen and made from “premium materials,” and they genuinely look great. What qualifies as “premium” ranges from aluminum to carbon fiber. Of course, each has the instantly iconic Glowbar somewhere on the cover, flashing when the laptop is opened or closed.

In essence, Googlebooks run Android, for better or worse. Googlebook OS is almost a parallel operating system, but it and mobile Android go hand-in-hand by design. By nature, that means Google didn’t intend to pack these with discrete graphics cards that could power most games. But that’s why GeForce Now exists, right?

Nvidia announced that GeForce Now would be coming to Googlebooks in an official capacity before the year is up. The original statement only specifies it will arrive “later this year,” which leaves a gap of around three months.

	

That doesn’t mean GeForce Now won’t work with Googlebooks when they become available in October. Google Chrome and even Firefox now support GeForce Now natively through the browser. That means logging into the game streaming website will present a similar experience to a fully dedicated Googlebook app.

Still, an app will likely be a better experience tailored to the hardware outfit Google and its partners pack into the new laptops.

This was expected for a couple of reasons. Google has partnered with Nvidia in the past, and Chromebooks were one of the main targets for GeForce Now in the early days. On top of that, when Googlebooks were first shown off, the majority of titles seen were via GeForce Now and not running on native hardware.

GeForce Now also announced today that a slew of new titles are getting support this week:

Stick It to the Stickman

title: Honor Magic 9 Pro Max goes official with 8,800 mAh battery, ARRI cameras, Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6
snippet: Honor has officially announced its latest flagship in China, with the Honor Magic 9 Pro Max packing powerful specs, upgraded cameras, the latest Snapdragon chip, and confirmed for an global launch later on. more…
fullText:
Honor has officially announced its latest flagship in China, with the Honor Magic 9 Pro Max packing powerful specs, upgraded cameras, the latest Snapdragon chip, and confirmed for an global launch later on.

The Honor Magic 9 Pro Max is an all-out flagship with a heavy focus on its cameras, so let’s start there.

Continuing its ARRI partnership that debuted on the Robot Phone, the Magic 9 Pro Max packs a 200MP main camera with “gimbal-level stabilization,” a 200MP telephoto camera with 3.5x optical zoom, and a 50MP ultra-wide camera. Those are arranged on the back in the style of an ARRI cinema camera, and they’re also tuned by ARRI to produce better colors both in photos and videos. Honor is also building out additional hardware including two teleconverter lenses and a “Mobile Video Kit” in partnership with SmallRig.

The front-facing camera is no slouch either, with a 55MP sensor that’s paired with a 3D depth sensing camera for face unlock.

	

The phone surrounding those cameras packs a punch too. 

Honor Magic 9 Pro Max is powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 and starts at 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage. Honor is using its own “Imaging Chip H1” to enhance camera processing, with MagicOS 11 based on Android 17 also available out of the box (with all its Liquid Glass-y-ness). The display is a 6.8-inch 2868×1320 OLED panel with Honor’s NanoCrystal Shield on top (which is both anti-scratch and anti-reflective), 10,000 nits of peak brightness – somehow –, 1-120Hz adaptive refresh rate support, and a 4,320Hz PWM dimming rate for better eye comfort. There’s an 8,800 mAh battery inside with 100W wired charging and 80W wireless, and the whole phone has IP68, IP69, and IP69K dust/water resistance ratings.

6.8-inch 2868×1320 LTPO OLED display, NanoCrystal glass, 4,320Hz PWM, 10,000 nits peak brightness

8,800 mAh battery, 100W wired charging, 80W wireless charging

IP68/IP69/IP69K

The Magic 9 Pro Max is available today in China, but Honor says global availability is coming soon. Europe, MEA (Middle East & Africa), SEA (Southeast Asia), and “other key international markets” are all confirmed at this point, but there’s no reason to expect this one in the US. 

Honor also launched the Magic 9 in China.

It has a similar design but with a smaller 6.37-inch display, Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, a very similar camera array, and an 8,000 mAh battery.

title: Pet Hair Everywhere? This $30 Roller Removes It From Places a Vacuum Simply Can’t
snippet: The SandBar helps in the battle against pet hair and rogue bits of kitty litter.
fullText:
Among the many joys of having a cat is the daily battle with the mess they leave behind. No matter what you try, finding litter and pet hair on furniture or in your bed is inevitable — either they track it in, or you do. If you’re a pet parent like me, this means searching for additional bits of litter and stray hairs that find their way into places you really don’t want them, including the bed. Short of pulling the sheets off entirely, few fixes exist.

I took a chance and tested the SandBar Roller, a $30 dual-roll lint roller, to see if it can make it easier to keep stray hair and litter at bay. I also put it through the paces for other lint-roller tasks like dusting and cleaning floors. Here’s how it fared.

How SandBar Roller differs from other lint rollers

The SandBar Roller Starter Kit I tested included the roller head, an extendable handle and two preinstalled lint rolls.John Carlsen/CNET

The SandBar Roller’s appeal lies in its two large lint rollers instead of one. While the idea doesn’t seem like much of a departure from a typical large lint roller, I couldn’t find any other dual-roller designs intended for use between bedsheets like SandBar. By arranging the rollers in this way, SandBar can clean the top and bottom sheets simultaneously without getting stuck.

			

More from CNET

	

			

	

			

									

						The Best Handheld Vacuums, Tested by CNET					

							

		

While SandBar markets its proprietary lint rolls as stronger than normal rolls, they’re not much different from what you’ll find on the extra-large pet hair version of the Scotch-Brite lint roller. Both are 8 inches wide, with an inner diameter of 1.5 inches. Much to SandBar’s credit, its six-pack of refill rolls is just $20, which is very competitive with other lint roll refills I found on Amazon, with the optional subscription price dropping to just $16 for each one-, two- or three-month delivery.

Testing the SandBar Roller

The extendable handle is very practical.John Carlsen/CNET

Ostensibly, this design targets coastal homes, where sand gets everywhere — hence the SandBar name. While I don’t live on the coast, I’ve experienced sand in my bed while traveling, or after day trips to the desert, and cat litter is a near-daily occurrence. With that in mind, I conducted a series of informal tests to see how the SandBar Roller holds up.

Upon putting SandBar between the sheets, I noticed it moved fairly smoothly, at least until it snagged on some sheets that were too loose. It didn’t jam, but that means it works better for beds with the sheet firmly tucked at the foot — something I don’t do for various sleep-friendly reasons. Still, it worked well after tightening the sheets a bit, even snagging a few cat hairs and litter fragments. It’s a nice alternative to washing the sheets as frequently as I have to now.

I like the stickiness of the rolls, which is satisfyingly tacky without leaving residue or making it difficult to pull off used strips.John Carlsen/CNET

The SandBar removed cat fur from hard-to-reach places

Next, I wanted to see how it handled cleaning smart window shades and curtains, which often collect fur as my cat patrols windows a few times a day. It was a little more awkward, but taking the handle off proved effective, and the sticky roller collected a substantial amount of fur. I had to peel off multiple sheets because of the amount of fur, but it took only a few passes to clean the curtain. The SandBar Roller was very useful on furniture and pet beds, but I noticed that being too aggressive can occasionally dislodge a roll.

The SandBar Roller left a fairly clean surface when I dusted off a TV cabinet and soundbar. Still, I wouldn’t trade it out for the duster and handheld vacuum I usually use. Likewise, it did well on the linoleum floor and carpet near my cat’s litter box, but still I prefer the cleaner result I get from vacuuming.

Should you buy the SandBar Roller?

The specialized design does its job well, but is probably too niche for people who aren’t pet parents or near vast swathes of sand.John Carlsen/CNET

At $30, the SandBar Roller is unlikely to break anyone’s budget, especially when you can find similarly large bed lint rollers for the same price. In that context alone, including the cost of refill rolls, it’s probably as good as any other option. Still, the dual-roll design’s ability to get between sheets is a compelling reason to consider the SandBar Roller over the competition. The design suits households that typically deal with a lot of sand and litter in the beds. I could even see myself taking it camping for quick dirt cleanup in a sleeping bag.

However, I wouldn’t recommend it for short-term beach house rentals because it cuts corners — new guests expect clean sheets when they arrive. That said, making a SandBar Roller available during a guest’s visit could be worthwhile to improve their experience, as long as you leave instructions explaining what it’s for and how it works.

If you don’t need the second roll — and mainly deal with pet hair on furniture — the ChomChom Roller doesn’t need refill rolls, making it a much better option for $25. Likewise, a handheld vacuum can do the same job with a bit more flexibility around the house — though it’s not quiet enough to use when others are sleeping. While it’s nice to have so many options, it’s always worth going with what works best for your needs and situation.

title: iOS 27 brings three key new features to Find My
snippet: iOS 27 brings new features to almost all of Apple’s apps, including Messages, Apple Music, Wallet, and more. Apple’s Find My app has its own share of changes in iOS 27. Here’s everything new. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 brings new features to almost all of Apple’s apps, including Messages, Apple Music, Wallet, and more. Apple’s Find My app has its own share of changes in iOS 27. Here’s everything new.

iOS 27: What’s new for Find My?

Apple touts three changes to Find My in iOS 27:

More flexible sharing options

UI enhancements

Apple Watch updates

First, more flexible sharing options in Find My give you more control over when and for how long you share your location with others. “Share your location for a custom duration or until a set date and time,” Apple says. You can also now “pause sharing with people individually, whenever you want.”

One of the bigger changes here is that you can now hide your location from a specific person without sending them any notification or alert. The other person won’t be notified when you pause, stop, or resume sharing your location with them.

Previously, you could turn off your location in the Find My app altogether, which wouldn’t send a notification. This, however, hid your location from everyone. In iOS 27, you can disable your location for specific people. 

To manage this, you’ll see a new “Hide Location” toggle on each person’s card in the Find My app. If you pause sharing your location with someone, they will see a “No Location Found” message in their Find My app.

Design changes

As for the UI enhancements, Find My in iOS 27 has been refreshed with a new Liquid Glass interface. The app largely missed out on Liquid Glass in iOS 26, but this year it has a new tab bar design that matches Apple’s other apps.

The Find My interface now also shows more specific location information on the app’s main page. This means you don’t have to tap on each person to view exactly what street they’re on at any given moment.

There is also new iconography in the Find My app in iOS 27. The “Items” tab, for example, is now denoted by a new AirTag-style icon.

Apple Watch updates

Finally, for cellular Apple Watch users, sharing your location will automatically use your Apple Watch when you’re away from your iPhone or iPad. 

Also on Apple Watch, there’s a redesigned, unified Find My app that integrates people, items, and devices into one interface.

title: iPhone video stabilization continues to wow me in the iPhone 18 Pro
snippet: I first talked about how much iPhone video stabilization impressed me when I tested it on the iPhone 13 Pro back in 2021. It’s been improved significantly since then, with both the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro having a version Apple refers to as “ultra-stabilized video.” While it doesn’t sound as sexy as some features, it makes a massive difference to the usability of the iPhone for handheld shooting – and my latest test really drove home just how good it is today … more…
fullText:
I first talked about how much iPhone video stabilization impressed me when I tested it on the iPhone 13 Pro back in 2021. It’s been improved significantly since then, with both the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro having a version Apple refers to as “ultra-stabilized video.”

While it doesn’t sound as sexy as some features, it makes a massive difference to the usability of the iPhone for handheld shooting – and my latest test really drove home just how good it is today … 

I have a mini tripod and GorillaPod that I carry with me when I know I’m going to want to shoot some iPhone video footage, but of course, one of the huge benefits of an iPhone is that it’s the camera you always have with you. There are times when I spot an opportunity for a shot and don’t have a tripod with me. 

It’s often possible to improvise, whether that’s by leaning the iPhone against a railing or bracing myself against something like a lamppost. But there are times when I rely on the built-in video stabilization on iPhones, and in the most recent example, shooting with the iPhone 18 Pro, I was incredibly impressed. 

A riverboat trip down the Thames demonstrated that there are times when the iPhone’s built-in video stabilization feature is actually better than a tripod. That’s because the boat rocks around a fair bit, which would have meant a stable shot of the boat with the scenery outside moving around. The iPhone reliably stabilized to the outside world with the boat moving around in the foreground.

That ability to keep the horizon true no matter what movements the platform makes is something we don’t even get with a typical gimbal. Most consumer-grade ones smooth out movement rather than eliminating it. It’s only with high-end professional gimbals and the type of giro mount designed for marine and helicopter use that we get truly locked horizons.

The iPhone 18 Pro’s ultra-stabilization feature honestly delivers this level of performance, and that’s a pretty incredible feature to have as standard in the stock Camera app with no external hardware required.

Check out the sample footage below. If you don’t want to take the full ride, the Tower Bridge section starting here is probably the best showcase for the feature. But if you do want to enjoy the London tourist experience, hit C to switch on the captions for all the bridge names and a few other comments, including pointing out Apple’s UK campus.

title: iPhone Duo video shows left-handed use for new model
snippet: iPhone Duo is less than a month away, but many prospective buyers are still wondering how well the device will work in left-handed use. Here’s a video that shows a left-handed example. more…
fullText:
iPhone Duo is less than a month away, but many prospective buyers are still wondering how well the device will work in left-handed use. Here’s a video that shows a left-handed example.

Here’s how iPhone Duo works in left-handed use

If you’re left-handed, the iPhone Duo may be exciting but also spark some questions. That’s because the new foldable is clearly designed for right-handed use primarily.

When using the outer display, iPhone Duo’s left side is one straight flat edge because it’s where the hinge is. But the right side has curved corners, inviting you to open it like a book.

The dock is also located on the right side of the display, and Apple hasn’t said if an accessibility setting will let you move it to the left.

So how will left-handed users fare with the iPhone Duo? 

Since everyone’s hand size is different, testing the device in an Apple Store will be the only way to know for sure. But I recently came across a video of iPhone Duo being used left-handed, and it’s the first time I’ve seen someone try it.

Here’s the video from Tom Hitchins (@bytereview) on Instagram:

Hitchins looks a little uncomfortable with the device, but as he explains in the comments, that’s because he’s actually right-handed. Thus, his left-handed test was for others’ sake.

	

The video says “works well enough” as Hitchins is able to reach from the left side all the way to the dock on the right. But you’ll want to test yourself to be sure.

I’m right-handed, but use my iPhone in my left hand so that my dominant hand is kept free. I suspect there are plenty of other right-handed users who do the same. So I’m a little unsure about the adjustment to using iPhone Duo in my right hand, but will report back once I’m able to test it.

title: Apple Wallet in iOS 27 adds feature that’s been on my wishlist for years
snippet: iOS 27 adds a variety of new features and changes for Apple Wallet, including one that’s been on my wishlist for years: the ability to import physical passes. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 adds a variety of new features and changes for Apple Wallet, including one that’s been on my wishlist for years: the ability to import physical passes.

iOS 27 lets you import physical passes, membership cards, event tickets into Apple Wallet

Apple Wallet offers a host of features to help you replace your physical wallet and keys.

It holds credit cards, driver’s licenses, transit cards, boarding passes, event tickets, car keys, home keys, hotel keys, and more.

And with iOS 27, the Wallet app takes another big step toward being the only wallet you need.

That’s because you can now import physical passes, tickets, membership cards, and the like into Apple Wallet.

Here’s how it works, per Apple:

iPhone and Apple Watch users will be able to create and store passes in Apple Wallet from physical cards, like loyalty or membership cards, eliminating the need to fumble through pockets and bags. With Siri mode in the Camera app, users simply point their iPhone at any physical card with a barcode or even screenshot a digital one, and they’ll be prompted to save it to Apple Wallet. Users can also create and add a pass directly from Apple Wallet. Once added, passes are ready to present as a barcode or QR code right from their iPhone or Apple Watch.

Digital passes are a lot more common today than when Apple Wallet first launched. But they aren’t available for everything.

I definitely still encounter businesses and events that utilize physical passes exclusively. And when I do, it adds a little anxiety to my life because I then need to remember to bring those passes with me at the right time.

But with iOS 27, everything can start going in the Wallet app, which is always with me. By putting everything in Wallet, the mental burden of remembering to bring something extra is suddenly gone.

Are there any physical passes you’ve added to Apple Wallet in iOS 27? Let us know in the comments.

title: Qualcomm announces the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6
snippet: Qualcomm today announced the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 to power the next generation of Android smartphones. more…
fullText:
Qualcomm today announced the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 to power the next generation of Android smartphones.

The big change this year is how there are a pair of chips. Qualcomm considers both to be “flagship” offerings that give “OEMs greater choice.” The Elite Gen 6 is seen as the follow-up to last year’s Elite Gen 5, while the Elite Extreme Gen 6 comes in a level higher.

Both are built on a 2nm process with an Oryon CPU that has two 5GHz Prime Cores and six 4GHz Performance cores. The 8 Elite Gen 6 offers 10% improved CPU performance and a 37% gain in power efficiency compared to the Gen 5. 

On the 8 Elite Extreme, CPU performance improves by 13% compared to last generation. A global VVC (H.266) codec on the Extreme allows for more power-efficient video. 

	

A “rearchitected” Adreno GPU offers 35% improved GPU performance and 40% power efficiency improvement over the Gen 5.

On the Extreme, there are AI-dedicated Adreno matrix cores that allow for more advanced models to run. GPU performance improves 44% compared to last year. There’s also 18 MB of High Performance Memory that compared to last generation offers a 12% power improvement. For gaming, Adreno Neural Fusion uses the new GPU matrix cores for AI super-resolution and frame generation, which makes possible up to 40% power savings in supported games.

The Hexagon NPU features a new Element Accelerator for transformer workloads to benefit LLMs. There’s 14% improved NPU performance and 20% improved AI performance-per-watt with the 12 scalar + 8 vector + 1 tensor + 1 element configuration.

On the 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, a 50% larger shared memory allows for 30B+ parameters Mixture of Experts (MoE) models. The aim is to reduce trips to external memory, with 35% improved NPU performance and 33% improved AI  performance-per-watt. 

The Spectra ISP features what Qualcomm calls Intelligent Pixel Control to understand scenes on a per-pixel level. On the Extreme, you have support for 8K60 video and 4K240 ultra HD slow-motion capture. 

Both chips are paired with the Qualcomm X105 5G modem that is “newly architected” for greater downlink (10% increase) and uplink speeds. Specifically, six antennas can capture multiple data streams at once. This supports 3GPP Release 19 5G Advanced.

Motorola today announced the Signature 27 with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. More on that here.

Note: Qualcomm paid for travel and accommodations for this launch event, but had no input on editorial content.

title: Google Messages finally rolls out new long-press menu with precise copying
snippet: After testing got underway in January, Google Messages is finally widely rolling out a new long-press menu in conversations. more…
fullText:
After testing got underway in January, Google Messages is finally widely rolling out a new long-press menu in conversations.

This new design replaces the top toolbar that housed various actions. Google only surfaced three actions with everything else in an overflow menu.

	

Upon long-pressing on a chat message or image, Google will show a floating menu with Remix (photos), Reply, Forward, Copy (text), Star, Delete, Select more, Info, and Save (photos).

Each action is accompanied by an icon at the front for quick scanning, while Copy lets you highlight a specific part of the message by pressing down and dragging the bubble. Previously, you could only copy the entire message.

	

If you’ve selected the newest message in a thread, Google will somewhat center it with a bouncy animation and haptic feedback. Messages prominently blurs the background layer when this menu is active. The row of emoji and “Create” Photomoji shortcuts is unchanged.

As of today, we’re seeing the new Google Messages long-press menu widely rolled out with stable version 20260910_03_RC02. There is a server-side component, so be sure to Force stop from the App info menu if it’s not yet live.

title: Motorola’s wide Galaxy Z Fold 8 competitor might be very tiny and called ‘Razr Flex’
snippet: According to a new leak, Motorola’s upcoming entry in the wide, book-style foldable space may be called “Razr Flex” and pack some very familiar specs. more…
fullText:
According to a new leak, Motorola’s upcoming entry in the wide, book-style foldable space may be called “Razr Flex” and pack some very familiar specs.

Specs for Motorola’s wide foldable were shared by Android Headlines alongside a possible name for the device – “Razr Flex.” That’s apparently the name being used internally around the device, so it’s unclear if that would be used as a consumer-facing name. The codename is “Parker,” the report claims.

Much more interesting are the details around the side of this foldable, which shares the same general form factor as Samsung’s smash hit Galaxy Z Fold 8, just in a much smaller footprint. Apparently, the outer display is just 4.97-inches in size – the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is 5.5-inches – while the inner display is less than 7-inches across. Very tiny by modern phone standards, even in this new form factor.

The leaked specs include:

	

4.97-inch outer display (1736×1140)

6.92-inch inner display (2364×1728)

110x149x5.8mm unfolded | 110x76x12.6mm folded

215g

Snapdragon 8 Gen 5

12GB RAM

256GB of storage

5,000 mAh battery with Qi2 (magnets unclear)

IP48/49

50MP main/50MP ultrawide rear cameras, 32MP selfie cameras

PANTONE Coriander, PANTONE Dark Botanical Garden

It’s important to stress just how much smaller this is compared to other wide foldables. iPhone Duo is thicker and heavier than Samsung’s phone, but has roughly the same screen sizes. The closest comparison is the Xiaomi 18 Fold, which has a 5.38-inch outer display, but even that still has a 7.58-inch inner panel. 

The specs are otherwise pretty familiar to the full-size Razr Fold that launched earlier this year.

Concept renders were also shared, but they’re explicitly not based on, well, anything except sketches and Motorola’s general design language – take them not just with a grain of salt, but maybe a whole container.

The “Razr Flex” is said to be launching this year with a “mid-December” debut mentioned.

title: Pixel Buds app update lets Gemini control audio and settings
snippet: With the Pixel 11 launch, Google promised a big Pixel Buds update in September. We’re now starting to see Gemini audio controls with the latest Pixel Buds companion app update. more…
fullText:
With the Pixel 11 launch, Google promised a big Pixel Buds update in September. We’re now starting to see Gemini audio controls with the latest Pixel Buds companion app update.

After updating to version 1.0.981607934 of the Pixel Buds app, we’re seeing @Pixel Buds in Gemini as the latest Connected App. You can control “settings like EQ preset, ANC mode, conversation detection, and touch controls.”

Hey Google, turn up the bass

Hey Google, turn on noise cancellation

This brings up the Gemini overlay, with a “Connecting to Pixel Buds” message appearing along with verbal confirmation.

On devices without the app update, those commands just open the system Bluetooth settings page.

	

We’re seeing Pixel Buds 1.0.981607934 widely rolled out via the Play Store today.

The three other features Google previewed presumably require a firmware update. The Pixel Buds Pro 2 will get Dynamic ANC that adjusts to “compensate when subtle shifts in the seal happen,” like if the buds move in your ear. There’s also Pixel Watch sleep sync that pauses music, disables touch controls, and silences notifications on the Pixel Buds. Finally, you will be able to trigger Live translate by tapping your Pixel Buds.

title: Samsung open-ear Galaxy Buds On images show what they look like when worn
snippet: Once rumored to go by a different name, Samsung’s Galaxy Buds On open-ear designs have appeared with a little more detail in new images, suggesting these earbuds might become official sooner rather than later. more…
fullText:
Once rumored to go by a different name, Samsung’s Galaxy Buds On open-ear designs have appeared with a little more detail in new images, suggesting these earbuds might become official sooner rather than later.

The Galaxy Buds On have been leaked several times over the last couple of months, though rumors suggested the earbuds would go by “Galaxy Buds Able” instead of the “Galaxy Buds On” name. That information was gleaned from Samsung’s Wearable app in early July, though the first of the two names seems to be an internal moniker.

New images of the Galaxy Buds On have surfaced (via Android Headlines). Previously, we’ve seen detailed renders and icon images, but nothing that looks like it could be official from Samsung. The new photos look a little cleaner, and one looks likely to be from the marketing team.

The Galaxy Buds On images also show what they look like when worn properly – that is, clipped around the ears rather than resting in them. It’s also a different style from the open-ear design worn over the ear. They look uncomfortable, but the design is already plentiful in certain regions, suggesting it’s a popular form factor.

	

It’s hard to pick up any details from the earbud images or to determine which port is the driver and which is the microphone for ambient noise detection. Even if that were determined properly, there’s no telling how they’ll sound prior to release.

The Galaxy Buds On were reported to have a few interesting features when previous images were leaked, such as an “Auto Volume” setting and head-nod and shake gesture control. Samsung Galaxy users will also have voice memos automatically transcribed to text.

Other devices like the Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra have been circulating alongside the Galaxy Buds On, suggesting Samsung is gearing up for another launch soon. When that is, there’s no telling right now.

title: Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra leak shows another side, confirming minimal changes
snippet: The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra showed up in a leak in August, but a new one has surfaced as the October launch date gets closer. The most recent images further confirm little about the design will change. more…
fullText:
The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra showed up in a leak in August, but a new one has surfaced as the October launch date gets closer. The most recent images further confirm little about the design will change.

The last leak image we saw of the Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra confirmed the new tablet will carry on Samsung’s recent camera notch design change. It takes on a teardrop shape, minimizing its scree footprint. That, along with the S Pen changed with the release of the Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra.

In comparing leaks with new ones courtesy of Evan Blass on Twitter/X, it still seems like nothing on the outside is being altered. The new leak provides side and rear views – something the previous leak left out. But it only further confirms the Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra will carry on the Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra’s build design.

That even goes for the S Pen charging location, which docks to the top right, when the Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra is in its landscape orientation.

	

That carry over from last year isn’t a bad thing, and tablets have sort of stagnated for some time. That’s part of the reason foldables have become so popular in recent years.

But Samsung has stuck to this design philosophy for some time. It might be nice to see some change that improves on bezels, or battery life. Of course, this leak only shows off what’s on the outside.

The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra is expected to launch on October 7.

In recent years, Macs had been getting more and more affordable. Cheaper starting points, more memory and storage per dollar, and the introduction of MacBook Neo. For the first time, Apple had started to become one of the best values on the market.

Unfortunately, Apple just drastically increased its prices because of the ongoing memory shortage. Macs aren’t as appealing as they were a few months ago, that said, there’s still some decent deals out there – and if you’re in need of a new computer, I’d still say todays Macs are a good value against the rest of the computing market.

MacBook Air

Up until the launch of MacBook Neo, the MacBook Air represented the entry point to Apple’s laptop lineup. Despite MacBook Neo making its value proposition slightly questionable, I’d still say MacBook Air is a great laptop if you want a better experience without needing anything premium.

MagSafe, a P3 color display, Center Stage on the webcam, and more battery life are just a few of the highlights with MacBook Air. It also comes with a 15-inch size variant, unlike MacBook Neo which only offers 13-inch.
